clean_body: A recap of the past year | | One year ago today, we launched this campaign to flip TN-02 and serve our neighbors. I knew then that many people would think this was a waste of time, energy, money - mine and others. That there would be a chorus of naysayers at every turn. What I hoped for, but wasn't assured of, was that there would be much, much larger chorus of people showing up every single day to put in the work for a better future for ourselves and our neighbors. And that's exactly what happened. Over this past year, together we have: Raised over $600,000 \- all from individual, grassroots donors (and 82% from within our district!) Had over 1300 people sign up to volunteer on this campaign. Invested in East TN by employing 20 East Tennesseans as well as hired local artists, printers, designers, venues, photographers, videographers, security, translators, and countless others. Held donation drives for warming centers, community clothing resource centers, teachers and educators, food banks, and more. Reached over 155,000 voters with texts, postcards, canvassing, friend banking, and phone banking. Held packed events and town halls in every corner of the district, from Townsend to Cumberland Gap. And we've made naysayers into believers. Folks who thought it was never going to be possible now believing that it just might be , if we all give everything we can. I'm not just talking about money. Now is the time to give a little bit more - time, energy, resources. We can do this. I'll leave you with part of my remarks from one year ago: "I know a lot of you might be afraid to nurture that tender flame of hope in your bellies, because here in East Tennessee, we are no strangers to disappointment. You might be thinking - I want to believe that change is possible, I want to believe in you, but I just don't know if it is. After Trump was inaugurated, my mentor in DC who had fought through Trump 1.0 shared this advice with all of us in the office. He said: no one is going to tell you what to do. No one is going to give you a guidebook on how to fight back. There is no cavalry coming. We are the cavalry. That is our path to flipping the longest-held Republican district in the country, and ousting a politician who cares more about photo ops and flaming culture war conflicts than serving the people of East Tennessee. In practical terms, we start right now. We meet voters where they are and listen to their concerns and their pain points and what they hope for the future. We hold town halls in every corner of the district and don't shy away from hard conversations with people who disagree with us. We sit down for small listening sessions with workers, with farmers, with veterans, with teachers, with parents, with faith leaders, with immigrants, and with dozens of other groups so that we can have real, honest conversations about what is affecting our community and how we can figure out real solutions - and not just after the election, right now. We build a volunteer army, neighbors talking to neighbors, ready to knock doors, make calls, and spread the word. We grow our movement through each of us reaching out to everyone we know. And we are going to make this campaign joyful: potlucks, concerts, battle of the bands, and block parties. Spaces where politics can feel like hope and connection, not despair and divisiveness. That's how we flip the longest-held Republican district in the country. That's how we build not just a campaign, but a movement that people can't wait to join. We put our hope for this region, for our state, for our country - to work. We put hope to work." And friends, that is exactly what we've done. See you out there ~ over the next five weeks. In gratitude and solidarity, Michaela P.S. See you at the~ at 1 p.m. at Urban Wilderness Gateway park in South Knoxville? | We have just over five weeks left to go. | | | Oregon didn't just adopt vote-by-mail. We INVENTED it. **So when President Trump signs an executive order restricting mail-in ballots, understand what that means: ** No state has more on the line than Oregon. This order isn't aimed at some abstract "voting system." **It targets how every single Oregonian votes.** Here's what Trump’s USPS order does. It orders the Postal Service to deliver ballots only to voters on a federal list — a list built by THIS administration. Their postmaster already said the quiet part out loud: states that don't hand over their voter data likely won't have mail ballots delivered at all. Now here's what I know. **I'm Oregon's chief elections officer. We have taken this administration to court — over their demand for your voter data, and over their first election order. We won/** _**They still are not stopping. **_ **The Constitution hasn't changed**. States run elections. Not presidents. Not postmasters. And this November, Oregon will run the same safe, fair, accurate vote-by-mail election we've run for 25 years — and I will use every power of this office to make sure of it. **[But fighting them in court is only one way to defend our elections. We must have the resources to communicate about what’s at stake — every lawsuit, every rule change, every attempt to rewrite how Oregon votes. That’s why I’m using my campaign to help travel around the state and talk directly to voters too. Chip in to help us keep fighting.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140067061/649426278/-569431239?refcode=260927-invented-rs&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDcvMS83NzI2MCIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICI2NTlhYWNiZS03YmJhLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=uYs1250ohE_NOEs4pE_wkkZC_dLQsLR_mcoz3oirzJU=)**

name: Chris Pappas
subject: Let me explain why this week’s deadline is so important
body:
[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1001&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]Chris Pappas for Senate[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/126?t=1002&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]Chris Pappas for Senate

This Wednesday’s FEC end-of-quarter deadline is the most important of the
entire campaign. Let me explain.

On September 30th at midnight, we face our final end-of-quarter deadline
before Election Day. Our campaign set a $1 million fundraising goal to
keep us on track for the final stretch, and here’s why:

📊 Republican John Sununu is surging ahead in polls.

📡 National Republicans are outspending us 3-to-1 on the airwaves.

🗳️ Every dollar that we raise today determines what we can budget for the
final 37 days until Election Day.

If we fall short now, we risk letting Republicans not only flip this seat
but lock up the Senate majority for a generation.

Granite Staters’ hard-earned Social Security. Lowering the cost of
healthcare. Reproductive rights.

That’s what’s on the line.

We can protect these priorities by beating Sununu in November. But only if
we raise the resources we need to compete.

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_2.lQJMJ0&refcode=em20260927-2&t=1003&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]I’m
directly asking you: Will you chip in $5 to help us reach
our end-of-quarter goal of $1 million and keep this seat from falling into
Republican hands?

[ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_2.lQJMJ0&amount=5&refcode=em20260927-2&t=1022&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]Donate $5 »

This $1 million goal isn’t arbitrary — it’s what we need to compete and
win over the next five weeks. If you’re able to help us reach it today, it
would be a massive help to everything we’re trying to accomplish. [ https://act.chrispappas.org/go/181?c0=em_ms_cp_20260927_2.lQJMJ0&refcode=em20260927-2&t=1023&akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr ]I
would be very grateful for your $5 contribution.

Thank you,

Chris

You can unsubscribe from this mailing list at any time:
http://act.chrispappas.org/cms/unsubscribe/unsubscribe/?akid=9161%2E582294%2EgkWBBr

I've spent over a decade of my life registering new Republican voters -- too many to count -- because I've learned one unshakable truth: nothing wins elections like having a bigger pool of voters than the Democrats. Not a mailer. Not a TV ad nobody watches. Not a "we'll match your gift" gimmick some consultant cooked up to squeeze one more dollar out of you. Just a voter registration activist with a clipboard and the determination to make sure every single Republican they meet is registered to vote and casts a ballot. With less than 50 days until Election Day, my organization Early Vote Action is staffing up in the swing states and critical races that will decide control of Congress. Just this week I'm deploying at least nine more voter registration staffers across four of the most competitive House districts in the country. Regular readers of _Navigating Uncertainty_ know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn't worked.
## [Global Multilateralism Is Dead](https://substack.com/redirect/f6e2bd4a-1d4f-4686-989d-ff5ec207f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

China is today far more autocratic than at any point in modern history, something the West, in its misguided approach to embracing China, has](https://substack.com/redirect/f6e2bd4a-1d4f-4686-989d-ff5ec207f7e7?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

## [Global Multilateralism Remains Dead](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

| | [Vikram Mansharamani](https://substack.com/profile/37278065-vikram-mansharamani)| | *

| September 27, 2025
[](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
[Two years ago I wrote an article entitled, "Global Multilateralism is Dead." The piece generated a lot of feedback, most of which was negative. Former colleagues from academia reached out to suggest my views were not helpful and global organizations stopped inviting me to speak at their gatherings. But the years since I penned the piece have delivered p...](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
| [| Read full story
---](https://substack.com/redirect/4417efc1-7e0b-4f71-b633-71ee3322f0ad?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that's killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world's biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can't have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn't address state-sponsored intellectual property theft?
Just this week, US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei delivered comments at the United Nations General Assembly describing the death of global multilateralism. Trump's tariffs, tirades against NATO, pullback from Europe, refocusing of US attention on the Western Hemisphere, and ~~willingness~~ preference for unilateral action have delivered the "post-WWII international order" body blow after body blow. And if you doubt this trend or Trump's intentions, listen to his blunt and defiant speech before the United Nations last week (link below).
[](https://substack.com/redirect/a47c2294-35ac-4f35-aeae-c4604d1751b6?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Trump took aim at multilateralism and global institutions. He called the International Criminal Court "full of evil people" with no jurisdiction over the United States and called on nations to withdraw from it. He attacked the UN Human Rights Council for focusing on the US while overlooking abuses elsewhere. He made clear that the United States would not subordinate its sovereignty to multilateral groups, and challenged other nations to follow suit.
Remarkably, Trump was not even the most vocal critic of the UN to speak at the UN during the general assembly. Argentina's Javier Milei took the same podium and made the American president sound like a polished career diplomat. The UN, Milei noted, was a "useless organization" that "only serves to feed a caste of parasites." The bodies charged with guaranteeing collective security and human rights, he argued, failed at the task and allowed chaos, violence, and international terrorism to flourish, while the self-appointed defenders of human rights sheltered dictatorships and regimes that brutalize women.
Milei's speech was stunning, and it's worth 20 minutes of your time (link below). He described the United Nations as a "bureaucratic leviathan devoted to deciding how the peoples of the world and their citizens should live" and thereby producing a curious hybrid of anarchy and tyranny. He suggested it was impotent toward those who break the most basic rules, and exerted Orwellian control over the liberal democracies that actually follow them.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/7ff8316a-1f0b-43f5-ad1a-2c36b0930010?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
But the most important line in Milei's speech was an eloquent caveat. Argentina, he said, will keep participating in multilateral forums in good faith but urged listeners to not "confuse cooperation with subordination." The objection isn't to nations working together. It's a rejection of a permanent class of officials nobody elected claiming authority over people who never consented to it, and to "cooperation" that has quietly hardened into a sense of "obligation" in conflict with sovereignty.
Ironically, the speeches were a sideshow. The real story was what happened in the hallways. On the sidelines of the General Assembly, Trump signed a _bilateral_ security agreement with Denmark and Greenland. He met with Venezuela's acting president and announced a _bilateral_ oil deal. He held one-on-one meetings with the leaders of Japan, Ukraine, and the GCC nations. The United Nations General Assembly has become a venue in which _bilateral_ deals get done...multilateral speech is theater, the bilateral meetings are the real work.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/750b3635-6590-4bee-aa0a-d8f0527d29aa?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Multilateralism has been withering for some time. The Abraham Accords were _bilateral_. The Iran war wasn't authorized by the UN. Pakistan's mediation between the US and Iran is _bilateral_. China's Belt and Road Initiative is a web of _bilateral_ deals. The European Union is struggling to hold together as Hungary and Poland resist Brussels on everything from migration to the rule of law. Everywhere you look, nationalism is resurgent and nation states are asserting their sovereignty.
So what replaces multilateralism? It's not chaos. It's transactional bilateralism, adorned in the language of national interest. Countries aren't withdrawing from the international order because they're isolationist. They're withdrawing because these institutions no longer serve their interests, and in many cases, actively work against them. Milei and Trump are the loudest voices, but there's a chorus of other leaders joining them. India's Modi, China's Xi, Turkey's Erdogan, and Italy's Meloni. are all prioritizing bilateral arrangements over multilateral commitments. The world is increasingly betting that sovereignty trumps solidarity.
The question, of course, is whether deal-by-deal arrangements can adequately address challenges that cross borders and impact the entire planet: climate change, pandemics, nuclear proliferation, the acceleration of AI, transnational terrorism and crime, and the regulation of the global commons. These problems don't respect borders. They require coordination at scale. The problem is the institutions designed to provide that coordination don't work.
[](https://substack.com/redirect/3ddbe001-8155-410a-81f1-77b3a7ea340f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
It's worth remembering, though, that we have run this experiment before -- and that the first attempt failed far more spectacularly. The League of Nations was born in 1920 out of Woodrow Wilson's conviction that collective security could replace the balance of power, and the US Senate promptly refused to join the institution its own president had designed. What followed was fifteen years of escalating humiliation. Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 and, when the League objected, simply walked out. Germany withdrew in 1933. Italy invaded Abyssinia in 1935, and the sanctions the League imposed were so carefully calibrated to avoid offending Rome that they excluded oil. The Soviet Union was expelled in 1939 for invading Finland, by which point there was scarcely anything left to be expelled from. Nor was the League an isolated failure. The Kellogg-Briand Pact of 1928, signed by more than sixty nations, outlawed war as an instrument of national policy exactly eleven years before the deadliest war in human history.
**The lesson is that multilateral institutions are not natural in a world defined by nation states. They are brief, fragile, and conditional, and they last precisely as long as their most powerful members find them useful ...and not one day longer.**
In 1975, Chevy Chase opened Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update with a running gag that became the show's first viral catchphrase. Every week, with mock seriousness, he would announce: "This just in: Generalissimo Francisco Franco is still dead."
[](https://substack.com/redirect/93889179-c647-4ae6-a9f6-eeb13b1584d4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
And so, at the risk of stealing his bit, I will say once again...**this just in: multilateralism is still dead.** Let it rest in peace. But let's be honest about the cause of death: not populism, but a lack of legitimacy the institutions never took seriously.
Abraham Lincoln set the standard at Gettysburg in a set of words that captured the essence of legitimacy in governance: "government of the people, by the people, for the people." Global multilateralism failed to incorporate this logic, instead building institutions of the elites, by the elites, and for the elites, staffed by people no voter chose and no voter can remove. As Milei noted, sovereign nations can still cooperate. They do it every day, and it has a name: _diplomacy_. But citizens of the world have spoken clearly over hundreds of years. They will only be governed by leaders they can fire. That clause is missing from every charter ever drafted, and until someone writes it in, multilateralism will keep dying -- over and over, in exactly the same way.

Trump and Millei continue hammering nails into the coffin. | | | Sep 27 | | | | | | | | | | | | | | ---|---|--- Regular readers of Navigating Uncertainty know that I have long felt that global multilateral institutions such as the United Nations are ineffective and, in many cases, work against the interests of their member institutions. While the concept of global governance to coordinate global responses for global challenges makes intuitive sense, it simply hasn't worked. | | | | ---|---|--- | July 24, 2023 | | | | | ---|---|--- | September 27, 2025 | Global multilateralism has lost all credibility. Do we really think the UN Security Council is useful when one of its members is the aggressor in a war that's killed millions? Or what about the World Health Organization, which refused to investigate the origins of COVID, the world's biggest public health challenge in a century? Surely we can't have faith in the World Trade Organization if it doesn't address state-sponsored intellectual property theft? Just this week, US President Donald Trump and Argentine President Javier Milei delivered comments at the United Nations General Assembly describing the death of global multilateralism. Trump's tariffs, tirades against NATO, pullback from Europe, refocusing of US attention on the Western Hemisphere, and ~~willingness~~ preference for unilateral action have delivered the "post-WWII international order" body blow after body blow. And if you doubt this trend or Trump's intentions, listen to his blunt and defiant speech before the United Nations last week (link below). Trump took aim at multilateralism and global institutions. He called the International Criminal Court "full of evil people" with no jurisdiction over the United States and called on nations to withdraw from it. He attacked the UN Human Rights Council for focusing on the US while overlooking abuses elsewhere. He made clear that the United States would not subordinate its sovereignty to multilateral groups, and challenged other nations to follow suit. Remarkably, Trump was not even the most vocal critic of the UN to speak at the UN during the general assembly. Argentina's Javier Milei took the same podium and made the American president sound like a polished career diplomat. The UN, Milei noted, was a "useless organization" that "only serves to feed a caste of parasites." The bodies charged with guaranteeing collective security and human rights, he argued, failed at the task and allowed chaos, violence, and international terrorism to flourish, while the self-appointed defenders of human rights sheltered dictatorships and regimes that brutalize women. Milei's speech was stunning, and it's worth 20 minutes of your time (link below). He described the United Nations as a "bureaucratic leviathan devoted to deciding how the peoples of the world and their citizens should live" and thereby producing a curious hybrid of anarchy and tyranny. He suggested it was impotent toward those who break the most basic rules, and exerted Orwellian control over the liberal democracies that actually follow them. But the most important line in Milei's speech was an eloquent caveat. Argentina, he said, will keep participating in multilateral forums in good faith but urged listeners to not "confuse cooperation with subordination." The objection isn't to nations working together. It's a rejection of a permanent class of officials nobody elected claiming authority over people who never consented to it, and to "cooperation" that has quietly hardened into a sense of "obligation" in conflict with sovereignty. Ironically, the speeches were a sideshow. The real story was what happened in the hallways. On the sidelines of the General Assembly, Trump signed a bilateral security agreement with Denmark and Greenland. He met with Venezuela's acting president and announced a bilateral oil deal. He held one-on-one meetings with the leaders of Japan, Ukraine, and the GCC nations. The United Nations General Assembly has become a venue in which bilateral deals get done...multilateral speech is theater, the bilateral meetings are the real work. Multilateralism has been withering for some time. The Abraham Accords were bilateral. The Iran war wasn't authorized by the UN. Pakistan's mediation between the US and Iran is bilateral. China's Belt and Road Initiative is a web of bilateral deals. The European Union is struggling to hold together as Hungary and Poland resist Brussels on everything from migration to the rule of law. Everywhere you look, nationalism is resurgent and nation states are asserting their sovereignty. So what replaces multilateralism? It's not chaos. It's transactional bilateralism, adorned in the language of national interest. Countries aren't withdrawing from the international order because they're isolationist. They're withdrawing because these institutions no longer serve their interests, and in many cases, actively work against them. Milei and Trump are the loudest voices, but there's a chorus of other leaders joining them. India's Modi, China's Xi, Turkey's Erdogan, and Italy's Meloni. are all prioritizing bilateral arrangements over multilateral commitments. The world is increasingly betting that sovereignty trumps solidarity. The question, of course, is whether deal-by-deal arrangements can adequately address challenges that cross borders and impact the entire planet: climate change, pandemics, nuclear proliferation, the acceleration of AI, transnational terrorism and crime, and the regulation of the global commons. These problems don't respect borders. They require coordination at scale. The problem is the institutions designed to provide that coordination don't work. It's worth remembering, though, that we have run this experiment before -- and that the first attempt failed far more spectacularly. The League of Nations was born in 1920 out of Woodrow Wilson's conviction that collective security could replace the balance of power, and the US Senate promptly refused to join the institution its own president had designed. What followed was fifteen years of escalating humiliation. Japan invaded Manchuria in 1931 and, when the League objected, simply walked out. Germany withdrew in 1933. Italy invaded Abyssinia in 1935, and the sanctions the League imposed were so carefully calibrated to avoid offending Rome that they excluded oil. The Soviet Union was expelled in 1939 for invading Finland, by which point there was scarcely anything left to be expelled from. Nor was the League an isolated failure. The Kellogg-Briand Pact of 1928, signed by more than sixty nations, outlawed war as an instrument of national policy exactly eleven years before the deadliest war in human history. The lesson is that multilateral institutions are not natural in a world defined by nation states. They are brief, fragile, and conditional, and they last precisely as long as their most powerful members find them useful ...and not one day longer. In 1975, Chevy Chase opened Saturday Night Live's Weekend Update with a running gag that became the show's first viral catchphrase. Every week, with mock seriousness, he would announce: "This just in: Generalissimo Francisco Franco is still dead." And so, at the risk of stealing his bit, I will say once again...this just in: multilateralism is still dead. Let it rest in peace. But let's be honest about the cause of death: not populism, but a lack of legitimacy the institutions never took seriously. Abraham Lincoln set the standard at Gettysburg in a set of words that captured the essence of legitimacy in governance: "government of the people, by the people, for the people." Global multilateralism failed to incorporate this logic, instead building institutions of the elites, by the elites, and for the elites, staffed by people no voter chose and no voter can remove. As Milei noted, sovereign nations can still cooperate. They do it every day, and it has a name: diplomacy. But citizens of the world have spoken clearly over hundreds of years. They will only be governed by leaders they can fire. That clause is missing from every charter ever drafted, and until someone writes it in, multilateralism will keep dying -- over and over, in exactly the same way. | | ---|---|--- VIKRAM MANSHARAMANI is an entrepreneur, consultant, scholar, neighbor, husband, father, volunteer, and professional generalist who thinks in multiple-dimensions and looks beyond the short-term. This past Friday, my former congressional colleague, Steve Stivers, and I published a new piece in the _Washington Examiner_ making the bipartisan case for permitting reform.
That may not sound like the most exciting topic, but it is one of the most fundamental. If we want to lower energy costs, build more housing, expand American manufacturing, modernize our infrastructure, and compete in AI, we have to get much better at actually building things.
You can read a preview below and read the full piece in the _[Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/87c75196-00af-4824-b9a4-9bd85e332499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_ here.
> Throughout **[American history](https://substack.com/redirect/dac02fcd-bd00-486b-ab56-d8e970973af2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , there have been moments when building on an enormous scale has been a national necessity. Think of how the New Deal brought electricity to **[rural communities](https://substack.com/redirect/bd11b8f1-df48-46fa-bce0-d3a8cb6da4e1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)** , or how two decades later, Dwight Eisenhower launched the Interstate Highway System, one of the largest public-works projects in our nation's history.
> We are entering another such moment for infrastructure in this country. After decades of relatively flat electricity demand, the United States is suddenly asking much more of its physical **[economy](https://substack.com/redirect/f884377f-88de-45d2-a86b-8e82f68d6f23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**. We need more housing in the places where people most want to live, more power for factories and businesses, and a stronger industrial base capable of supplying our military in an increasingly dangerous world. Competition with China raises the stakes further -- the race for leadership in artificial intelligence requires enormous amounts of electricity and computing capacity, as well as the infrastructure to support both.
Continue reading at the _[Washington Examiner](https://substack.com/redirect/87c75196-00af-4824-b9a4-9bd85e332499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)_[.](https://substack.com/redirect/87c75196-00af-4824-b9a4-9bd85e332499?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)

subject: Sleeping on NC = snatching defeat from the jaws of victory
body:
Roy can’t overcome the full force of the GOP’s dark-money machine on his own
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1445&source=&t=1&akid=3876%2E124072%2EO-pzBb) | | | |

[](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1445&amount=5&t=8&akid=3876%2E124072%2EO-pzBb)
Now looky here, Peter:
**Democrats have a snowball’s chance in hell of retaking the U.S. Senate majority this fall without flipping North Carolina’s red seat blue.**
Ain’t nobody’s done that since 2008, and right now, the GOP is flooding _beaucoup bucks_ into NC to keep it that way. That’s ‘cause having a proven winner like two-term former Governor Roy Cooper as the Democratic nominee is our best chance of flipping _any_ of the four seats we need.

**Derek, we're just days out from our last quarterly FEC deadline before the midterm elections.** We need 25,000 more contributions this month to hit our goal — and in a moment, I'm going to ask you to contribute before that deadline hits on Wednesday. But if that's all you need to hear, **[you can pitch in now](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/7929?t=14&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_092726_eoqdonorgoal&akid=10566%2E5257348%2EwrR-yu)** : | | [DONATE→](https://act.adamschiff.com/go/7929?t=15&amount=10&refcode=aschiff_email_092726_eoqdonorgoal&akid=10566%2E5257348%2EwrR-yu)
---
If you're not convinced, here's why this moment matters.
Wednesday's deadline is the last of its kind this cycle. I don't believe that MAGA billionaires should be calling all the shots. That's not how democracy is supposed to work.
**When we report our numbers to the FEC, it's proof of whether Democrats' grassroots movement is growing stronger — or standing still — as we head into November.**
Since Trump took office, I have led important efforts to investigate his corruption, force votes to end his illegal war, and demand accountability from this administration.
There is one check on this president that he cannot fire and cannot intimidate: a Democratic Senate, with the gavels and subpoena power to hold him to account.
That's why we're fighting to flip the seats that will decide the majority, because the evidence we uncover only matters if we win the power to act on it.
_I know we have the grassroots strength to win back the Senate this November. Democrats are making real gains in states where we weren't supposed to have a chance._
_Wednesday's deadline is about proving it._
**[Derek, if everyone reading this far pitched in $10, we'd meet our goal in no time. Don’t look at this as another fundraising pitch or one of those doomsday warnings. I hope this will instead give you a genuine glimmer of hope about what we're up against — and exactly how we're going to win. * * *
Hey folks,
The campaign to turn Andrew and Tristan Tate into victims is getting desperate.
Their lawyer, Joe McBride, is publicly attacking officials, comparing their situation to the Epstein scandal, and describing brutal conditions behind bars. But when you dig into what's actually being claimed--and what the court record says--a very different picture starts to emerge.
Here's what we get into:
* [**00:01:51**] McBride invokes Jeffrey Epstein while arguing the Tate brothers are being unfairly treated--and lashes out at the officials standing in their way.
* [**00:04:46**] We hear the claims about tiny cells, missing pillows, bad beds, and other conditions inside the Miami detention facility.
* [**00:07:05**] A medical expert enters the conversation, raising concerns about the brothers' nutrition and physical condition--and I break down why I'm skeptical.
* [**00:09:44**] The argument shifts from the Tates themselves to a bigger question: if prison conditions are unacceptable, why should reform only matter when powerful people are locked up?
* [**00:12:06**] We get to what I think is really driving this campaign: an effort to build enough political pressure to get powerful people to intervene.

This episode is about more than Andrew and Tristan Tate. It's about power, privilege, accountability, and what happens when people who built their identities around strength suddenly demand sympathy from the system. Prisoners deserve basic dignity. name: Jeff Bridges
subject: Weiser, walking, and wine on the Western Slope
body:
We started in the best way possible, with a canvass launch and hearing from voters about what’s making it harder to earn a good life in Colorado.

| | | | | | | [View this email in your browser](https://mailchi.mp/dff9ad66d8ba/get-more-smarter-on-colorados-budget-10379023?e=b48bb2b4f4)
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/h4JfVqDMLgl?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | | | | | | | | | | | | | | | Hi there,
Saturday started with door knocking in Grand Junction and ended with dinner in Montrose. In between we met with local small business owners, had a debate, and of course lots of driving.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/cA3KcUKKA9d?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| |
We started in the best way possible, with a canvass launch to knock doors and hear directly from voters about what’s making it harder to earn a good life in Colorado.
We had pretty good company! My friend and our next governor Phil Weiser joined us for the morning.

From there, we headed to Club 20 for a debate with my opponent, Kevin Grantham. Club 20 represents Colorado's 22 western counties, and I've hoped for a chance to debate on their stage for more than a decade.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/FyT0mjPzRpx?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | Kevin and I actually agree that Colorado has gotten too expensive. We also really respect each other, and it was a very cordial debate.
Where we disagree, pretty dramatically, is on what the Treasurer should do about our cost of living crisis.
Colorado's Treasurer manages billions of dollars on behalf of Colorado. I think anyone holding public office right now should pull every lever they have to lower the cost of living.
**For the Treasurer, that means putting more Colorado dollars to work here in Colorado.**
Housing working people can actually afford. Renewable energy to lower bills and fight global warming. Good-paying jobs across our state. All while protecting taxpayer dollars and earning a good return.
Kevin has a different vision for the office. "Less is more."
That’s what elections are for, and I'm grateful to Club 20 for offering us the chance to share those differences together on stage.
---
| | | | | | | | | | [|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/fpQZV3zGcwx?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | After the debate, I headed south toward Montrose, with a stop in Delta County to visit the team at Aquila Wineries in the North Fork Valley.
This is one of my favorite parts of traveling the state.
Aquila is building a business around something distinctly Colorado. Local agriculture, local craftsmanship, and a landscape you simply can’t recreate anywhere else.
And delicious wine.
When we talk about investing Colorado dollars in Colorado, this is part of what I mean. Strong local economies don’t appear by accident. They grow because people take risks, build businesses, create jobs, and invest in the places they call home.
---
[|
---](https://us.list-manage.com/DD4lMbUUh6h?e=b48bb2b4f4&c2id=bbe572662fdb5fed2d0855c1bcb00da8)
| | My last stop was the Montrose County Blue Tsunami dinner.
I've been to Democratic dinners in counties many times the size of Montrose with smaller crowds and a lot less energy. This room was packed.
Keep an eye on Montrose. Something is happening there.
Whether I’m knocking doors, debating the role of the Treasurer, visiting a local business, or talking with a packed room in Montrose, I keep hearing the same basic question:
**How do we make it a little easier to earn a good life in Colorado?**
For me, the answer's in the Treasurer's office. Still many more miles ahead before we get there. Thanks for being part of the journey.
---
| | Talk soon,
---
| | P.S. The peach cobbler at the Club 20 steak fry... chef's kiss. And little known fact: every member of the Mesa University board gets to design a cocktail for the restaurant at the Maverick Hotel!
---

subject: Trump’s rubber stamps for life:
disclaimer_text: Paid for by Demand Justice PAC
body:
[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20260927-61849&t=1001&akid=61849%2E1407376%2EztFG8o ]Demand Justice PAC[ https://act.demandjustice.org/go/54940?refcode=em20260927-61849&t=1002&akid=61849%2E1407376%2EztFG8o ]Demand Justice PAC

Trump is panicking.

He recently rushed to nominate a slew of judges to lifetime seats on the
federal bench — all at once, all ahead of the midterms.

Why? Because Trump knows Republican control of the Senate won't last. He
wants as many loyalists locked into lifetime positions as possible before
his majority is in jeopardy — especially judges who'll back him up in the
election disputes he's already threatening to bring.

Here's the scary part: every one of Trump's judicial nominees has dodged
the same questions. Who won the 2020 election? What happened on January
6th?

They won't answer, because the truth contradicts Trump's lies — and these
nominees have decided their loyalty to a wannabe authoritarian matters
more than ruling with independence under the Constitution.

body:
This is the last End-of-Quarter deadline before Election Day.

[ CHIP IN NOW >>](https://us.list-manage.com/nMRjHqKwYBf?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Peter,
It's that time again, and this time, _it's the last one._
At the end of every three months, campaigns across the country submit their fundraising totals to the Federal Election Commission (FEC). But these Quarterly Reports do a lot more than tell the FEC who donated.
_They're a campaign's report card._
They show the media, House leadership, and my opponent how healthy and competitive our campaign really is. **And Peter this is our FINAL End-of-Quarter report before Election Day.** There are no more chances after this. The final countdown has begun.
That's why we've set our most important goal yet: $25,000 before midnight on September 30.
[**HELP US HIT $25,000 BEFORE THE FINAL DEADLINE →**](https://us.list-manage.com/13SXu8HeiJa?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)
A strong report tells everyone watching that Central New York is ready for change, and that this seat is ready to FLIP. A weak one tells the Democrat Machine they can coast to November.
_I grew up in Auburn in a blue-collar family. I know what it means to work hard, do everything right, and still wonder why it keeps getting harder to get ahead. I'm running to lower costs, back law enforcement, protect our family farms, and give President Trump another reliable America First vote in the House._
But none of that happens unless we finish this race strong.
[**Will you chip in $26, $50, $100, or whatever you can to help us earn an A+ on our final report card?**](https://us.list-manage.com/VIuZFSQmIFF?e=7e42b80a6c&c2id=65ca27defa2b2ff4fbda44443b52d843)

Folks,
First of all, I want to say thank you.
Let me explain why:
This campaign has raised an extraordinary amount of money from an extraordinary number of people giving small-dollar, grassroots donations. That grassroots support is something that I'm grateful for every day. I promise you: **I never, ever take you or your support for granted.**
But the reality is that even with that unprecedented level of grassroots support, we still have critical fundraising goals to meet in the final stretch of this campaign to build the resources it'll take to win here in Georgia.
The Senate GOP's main Super PAC -- which is just one of many right-wing Super PACs who could spend money on this race -- has raised more than $500 million. And then there's still Trump and his Super PAC, plus other far-right billionaires like Elon Musk waiting in the wings.
The truth is that MAGA can spend endlessly attacking us because they've got an army of billionaires and corporate PAC donors lining up to fund the smears.
We expect to be outspent in this race, possibly by hundreds of millions of dollars. We don't need to match the Super PACs dollar for dollar, but we do need to make sure we get our message out.
**So please, I 'm humbly asking:**
**[Can you give $5 to my reelection campaign today to help me fight back against the dark money Super PACs who are going to flood Georgia with attacks? Donate today to fight their lies with the TRUTH >>>](https://substack.com/redirect/7573ecff-428f-4576-925d-b188e1c975d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Post _-Citizens United_ , Super PACs and secret money in politics are totally out of control, corrupting policymaking on behalf of the rich and powerful.
And when members of Congress aren't fundraising from lobbyists and corporate PACs, they're just trying to dodge getting bombed by these Super PACs.
Candidates all over the country are facing down hundreds of millions in Super PAC spending from dark-money groups that don't even disclose their donors until after the election, if ever.
_Is this the way we want our government to work? Do we really want to allow unlimited, secret political money to bend the nation 's agenda in darkness?_
All across Georgia and all across the country, a wave is building. The kind of wave that comes once a generation, when the people have been pushed too far and decide all together, all at once: **enough is enough.**
That is the message that we're going to send when we WIN this November.
Yes, this election will be tough.
But I know how to win tough fights. I've done it before.
_Let 's do it again._
**[Please, consider making a donation to my reelection campaign today. I wouldn 't ask if it didn't make a real difference.](https://substack.com/redirect/7573ecff-428f-4576-925d-b188e1c975d1?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
Thank you, sincerely, for chipping in if you can and for everything you do to support this campaign and this movement.
As always,

Meet Coach Tuberville:

**Coach Tuberville was born in Camden, Arkansas, the third of three children of Olive and Charles Tuberville. College Football’s 2004 Coach of the Year and two-time SEC Coach of the Year, Tommy Tuberville is most often recognized for his success on the field. But it is the legacy of his father, a highly decorated WWII veteran and Purple Heart recipient, that motivates Coach Tuberville to give back to the brave men and women of the United States Armed Forces.

In 1989 Coach Tuberville met his future wife, Suzanne Fette, at the Sugar Bowl in New Orleans. They were married in 1991 and have two boys, Tucker and Troy, who continue to make their dad proud.

In his career as a College Football Coach, Tommy started a long and successful career at the University of Miami, starting as a graduate assistant and rising to the Hurricanes' defensive coordinator. He led the Canes to three AP national championships and coached future Hall of Famers Ray Lewis and Warren Sapp, as well as Dwayne "The Rock" Johnson.

body:
A personal note from Marilyn.

---
| | My mother came to this country from Korea. Asian immigrants like her were barred from becoming American citizens until 1952. My grandmother was a Black woman in the South who faced poll taxes and literacy tests until the Voting Rights Act passed in 1965.

**That's not history to me. It's the reason I don't treat a ballot as a piece of junkmail.**

This February, the U.S. House passed a bill that would require documentary proof of citizenship, in person, to register to vote, and photo ID with every ballot.

In a vote-by-mail state like ours, that means putting a photocopy of your ID in the envelope, every election. I voted no. It hasn't passed the Senate.

Two weeks ago the chairman of the Senate committee said out loud that they'll try to move the core of it through the budget process instead, so it needs 50 votes - and no Democrats at all.

_I'll keep voting no. But I can only do that from this seat, and holding this seat takes a strong campaign because honestly, no one is safe when Republicans control everything in DC._

**Tomorrow at midnight our quarter closes and we file publicly. clean_body: A personal note from Marilyn. | | My mother came to this country from Korea. Asian immigrants like her were barred from becoming American citizens until 1952. My grandmother was a Black woman in the South who faced poll taxes and literacy tests until the Voting Rights Act passed in 1965. That's not history to me. It's the reason I don't treat a ballot as a piece of junkmail. This February, the U.S. House passed a bill that would require documentary proof of citizenship, in person, to register to vote, and photo ID with every ballot. In a vote-by-mail state like ours, that means putting a photocopy of your ID in the envelope, every election. I voted no. It hasn't passed the Senate. Two weeks ago the chairman of the Senate committee said out loud that they'll try to move the core of it through the budget process instead, so it needs 50 votes - and no Democrats at all. # [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
[](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260927_1_pete.3gemSK&refcode=em20260927-2250&t=1&akid=2250%2E299639%2ENiuMdj)
Hi Peter, it’s Pete Buttigieg.
I know you’re busy, so I will give you the bottom line up front: I’m reaching out today because I am proud to support Gina Hinojosa for Governor of Texas, I believe she will win, and [**I hope you’ll join me in supporting her by making a contribution to her campaign.**](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260927_1_pete.3gemSK&refcode=em20260927-2250&t=2&akid=2250%2E299639%2ENiuMdj)
Before I tell you more about why I know Gina can win in November, I want to share a story about how on-the-ground campaigning, combined with the right candidate, made history in Texas before.
In 1990, Ann Richards was down by double digits in the final months of her race for governor – before she went on to shock the political world with her victory. Now, all signs point to a similar shockwave this November.
Fast-forward to this past March, where Democrats turned out in record-breaking numbers for the primary.
In the months since, Gina Hinojosa has closed a 10-point gap against Greg Abbott and now holds a 4-point lead in the polls. That's the kind of movement you see right before a race breaks our way.
I think part of why Gina is breaking through is that she's not asking Texans to pick a side in some left-versus-right fight. She's asking a simpler question: is this right, or is this wrong? Is it right that the cost of living keeps climbing while the people at the very top get another tax break? Most Texans already know the answer, no matter who they've voted for in the past.
Gina has the momentum. Gina has voters ready to turn out for her. What she needs now, in these final six weeks, is the resources to reach every one of them – to get her message into every part of the state before Election Day, and to answer the attacks that are already coming her way.
**[So, I am asking you personally: Will you make a donation to Gina Hinojosa's campaign today and help her make history this November?](https://act.ginafortexas.com/go/1356?c0=em_ms_gh_20260927_1_pete.3gemSK&refcode=em20260927-2250&t=3&akid=2250%2E299639%2ENiuMdj)**

Thank you,
Pete Buttigieg

Friend of Life, Every day, women walk into PreBorn! Network Clinics carrying burdens most of us can hardly imagine. Many are frightened. Many feel alone. Nearly all of them are facing one of the most significant decisions of their lives. We believe every one of those women deserves the opportunity to slow down before making that decision. She deserves to see her baby on an ultrasound, hear the heartbeat, receive compassionate care, and encounter the hope of Jesus Christ. That's why friends of PreBorn! have stepped forward with an extraordinary commitment. They have pledged to **MATCH every gift made before September 30, up to $100,000** , because they want twice as many women to receive the care, support, and hope they so desperately need. Your gift doesn't simply become twice as large. It helps create twice as many opportunities for mothers to choose life. Twice as many opportunities to share the gospel. Twice as many opportunities for families to experience the kind of hope we've seen God provide time and time again. A gift of **$28 helps provide one life-saving ultrasound.** During this matching challenge, that same gift can help provide **two opportunities** for women to see their babies, hear the heartbeat, and receive compassionate care before it's too late. If you've been considering supporting PreBorn! for the first time, there has never been a better opportunity to make your generosity go even further. **Will you make your matched gift today and help reach twice as many women with life-saving ultrasounds and the hope of Jesus Christ?**

body:
We can reclaim a Democratic majority together.
# [](https://act.katieporter.com/go/9?t=1&akid=41585%2E3422442%2ELx3OJY)
It’s official – the path back to national sanity runs through our district, Virginia's Fighting Fifth!
**That’s right, the DCCC has elevated our race to the coveted Red to Blue status, given to the highest tier of pick-up opportunities needed to reclaim a Democratic majority.**
This is on top of the momentum we got from a great new poll that shows our months of barnstorming the district have paid off – we have pulled even with Rep. John McGuire in a district he won by 15 points less than two years ago. Better yet, when voters hear about his record, we pull away by ten points. That’s what happens when he sells out our communities to protect his 100% rating from the corporate lobbyists in DC.
**[If you love this momentum as much as I do, don’t bother reading the rest of this email. Just click here to split a donation between my campaign and Truth to Power so we can reach the voters who will do the rest. Let’s leave nothing on the table to ensure we reclaim this seat for the people of the Fighting Fifth.](https://act.katieporter.com/go/22230?c0=em_ms_ttp_20260927_1_ak.-mFxL7&refcode=em20260927-41585&amounts=5%2C20%2C50%2C100%2C250%2C500%2C1000&t=2&akid=41585%2E3422442%2ELx3OJY)**
So: what does being a Red to Blue race mean?
For one, it proves that the progress we keep telling you about – the progress that you have helped us build through grassroots, people-powered organizing – really works. And now, it has been recognized and rewarded.
The DCCC’s Red to Blue program is a highly competitive group of top-tier races across the country. Getting added to this list sends a big signal that this is the place to invest your time, talent, and treasure, if you want to reclaim our country from the kleptocrat-in-chief.
The path back to sanity runs through the Virginia Fifth and the defeat of John McGuire. He was part of January 6th, has been enriching himself day trading stocks, and is so extreme that he opposes a right to contraception. He has been AWOL from the district, while voting to shutter rural health clinics and labor and delivery units. He got caught insider trading stocks in companies impacted by his party’s work in Congress.
This news shows that a campaign like ours – one that rejects money from lobbyists and focuses on grassroots energy – can get the resources we need to flip this seat.
I’m proud that our grassroots campaign has already defied the odds. But being a Red to Blue race isn’t all sunshine and puppies – it also means that the Republicans’ dark money juggernaut will be unleashing on us soon. Big time.

I wish I could promise you things will turn around overnight.
But here's what I can tell you: There is no path to taking back the House this November unless we protect critical seats like KS-03. And with just 37 days to go until Election Day, the entire country is counting on us to do our part.
Listen, I know how frustrating it is for elected officials like me to ask for your hard-earned money, especially when you're putting more and more of your paycheck toward the bare necessities. I don’t take that lightly at all.
But whether we like it or not, winning these midterms — and putting our country back on the right track — doesn't come without a cost.
National Republicans and their billionaire allies have more money to spend than ever before. More resources to tip the scales in races like ours and install their hand-picked yes-men in my place.
So yes: I know this year has been hard, difficult, and infuriating. But that’s why we need to give these last few weeks EVERYTHING we’ve got — and with our last End-of-Quarter deadline just three days away, we can’t wait another moment to act.

name: Team Cooper
subject: Roy needs your help today
body:
This deadline is critical.
| [](https://act.roycooper.com/go/15912?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1444&source=&t=1&akid=3882%2E124072%2EQvr1Lk) | | | |
---
Peter – we know ... yet _another_ email.
We truly wish we didn’t have to send you so many, **but with the last FEC end-of-quarter deadline before the election coming up in just three days, we URGENTLY need your help.**
You see, GOP dark-money super PACs have already spent over $100 million on this race. Now, they’re watching VERY closely to see if we hit our fundraising targets. If we fall short, they’ll take it as a sign of weakness – and spend millions more to buy this seat for Michael Whatley.
That’s why we’re reaching out today. [**_The _only_ way Roy can stay competitive is if folks like you chip in now. Here’s why:_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1444&amount=5&t=8&akid=3882%2E124072%2EQvr1Lk)
The U.S. Senate race in North Carolina is one of the most competitive and expensive in the country. **Michael Whatley and his MAGA allies know we can’t flip the Senate blue if we lose this battleground seat, so they’re pulling out all the stops to win.**
That’s why President Trump and JD Vance both personally came to North Carolina recently to spread lies about Roy. It’s why far-right groups are spending millions on false attack ads against him. Peter, their schemes are working: **Two polls show this race is now statistically tied.**
Roy isn’t going down without a fight. He knows we can win this, but with the FEC deadline just a few days away – and the GOP outspending us at an alarming rate – we have to turn things around NOW. We need your help, Peter.
**Roy understands that it’s not possible for you to donate to every email we send – but we’re hoping you’ll pitch in to this one:[_If you’re able to support our campaign, will you donate to this email right now? Chip in $5 or whatever you can to help us expand our razor-thin lead, flip this must-win seat and take back the Senate majority. >>_**](https://act.roycooper.com/go/14264?refcode=email_fr_pros_jtk1444&amount=5&t=9&akid=3882%2E124072%2EQvr1Lk)

Peter, This week, the Cook Political Report, the most respected election forecaster in the country, called a Republican hold on the House "almost impossible." Texas Republicans can do that math, and the panic has already set in. James Talarico is pulling ahead in the Senate race, lifelong conservatives keep telling us they have had enough, and our campaign is growing in places Democrats have not competed in for a generation.

Shifts like this only happen when a campaign puts in the work every single day. Our movement goes everywhere, rural fence lines and suburban cul-de-sacs alike. Keith Self took the other road, holed up in Washington championing every disaster from the least popular president in the history of polling. Folks around here have noticed the difference. clean_body: More than eight to one| | | | = National Republican groups have already spent about $2 million this month to help elect my opponent, John Braun. That is more than eight times the amount spent to support our campaign. = That is not a warning about what might happen. It is the fight already landing on TV screens, phones, computers, and mailboxes across Southwest Washington. Will you donate $10 today to help my campaign answer that flood of outside money and keep our own message in front of voters? Mike Johnson’s House leadership super PAC alone has spent $1.19 million on digital and television ads against me. A Trump-linked super PAC has put another $2 million into this race. And more spending is expected before Election Day. They can buy a lot of noise. They do not get to buy Southwest Washington. I have won close races by showing up, telling the truth, and doing the work. This campaign answers to the people who live here—not Donald Trump, Mike Johnson, Elon Musk, or any national group writing checks from somewhere else. Every grassroots contribution helps us push back, reach more voters, and make sure the people deciding this race hear directly from me, not only from the groups trying to define us. = = This race has always come down to whether people decide their voice matters. clean_body: Counting on supporters like you to finish strong | Peter, If you can believe it, there are only three days left in September. Then it's a full-on sprint to Election Day. And we’re really in the thick of it, because the NDRC is running one of the most ambitious electoral programs we’ve ever mounted. Our goals are sweeping, and they have to be if we’re going to effectively counter the Republicans’ nationwide redistricting crisis. We’re targeting over 250 critical state-level races across the country where we can make the biggest impact in the long-term fight for fair maps and fair elections. And we’re setting an ambitious goal of 2,500 grassroots donations by Wednesday’s end-of-quarter deadline — the last one of these before Election Day — to help power our wide-ranging work. = | If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: = | = = | = = | = We’ve broken our priority states down into three core categories: 1. Places where we must DEFEND against the threat of future map manipulation. 2. States where we can pass ballot initiatives and elect Democracy Defenders to COUNTER the Republican power grab and level the playing field — so we can ultimately end gerrymandering for good. 3. And races in states where we can ADVANCE the power of pro-democracy leaders — by electing more legislators who can pass fairer maps, independent-minded judges who will protect democracy, and governors who can serve as a firewall against more GOP power grabs. We've seen what we're up against: a Republican Party determined to rig democracy to grant itself unearned, unchecked control over our whole country. We're 37 days away from Election Day, which means that you're probably getting bombarded with texts and emails from candidates. I hear about it from folks every day.
Trust me, I get it. But we wouldn't be reaching out if it weren't important, so I wanted to write to you personally, cut through the noise, and lay out exactly what's at stake this November.
Here in North Carolina, we can either go with Roy Cooper, a proven fighter who has done this:
* Protected and expanded affordable health care access
* Defended our fundamental rights and freedoms
* Made life tangibly better for working families

... or Michael Whatley, a former Big Oil lobbyist and ultimate Washington DC insider who has done that:
* Spread conspiracy theories about the 2020 election
* Served as President Trump's yes-man for years on end
* Appointed a convicted child sex offender to powerful leadership positions within the Republican Party

[Donate](https://substack.com/redirect/358fe803-fe51-4f5a-8499-6adb296428af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
When you put it like that, it isn't a close call or a hard decision. It's a choice between someone who's spent his career serving North Carolina and someone who's spent his career serving himself and his stock portfolio at the expense of North Carolinians.
But here's the tough part: We know that this race could come down to just a handful of votes, and Republican dark-money super PACs are already pouring over $100 million so far into attack ads filled with lies and distortions about Roy. Those PACs don't answer to voters and they don't have to tell the truth. They just have to spend enough money to make people doubt what they already know: that Roy Cooper is a trusted and proven public servant who has dedicated his career to fighting for hardworking North Carolinians.
So if you're ready to join a people-powered movement fighting for a better future, please consider [chipping in a few dollars before our last end-of-quarter deadline](https://substack.com/redirect/358fe803-fe51-4f5a-8499-6adb296428af?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), [signing up to knock doors](https://substack.com/redirect/3cab2fd4-309a-4aaa-bfde-6a93285e30f8?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), or [registering to vote](https://substack.com/redirect/21b46e39-39a2-4f58-b23e-6342c464744c?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Every effort adds up fast with the help of people like you.
Thank you,
Andy Volosky, Digital Director for Cooper for North Carolina

We'll hand Democrats their first statewide win in Texas since 1994, and the earthquake will be felt by Americans across the country. First, let's be clear about how we got here. The Republican establishment in DC spent over $150 million — the most expensive Senate primary in American history — trying to stop Ken Paxton from becoming the nominee. _They lost._ Paxton defeated Sen. John Cornyn by nearly 30 points. But the damage was done, and now Democrat James Talarico is within striking distance of flipping the seat. You'd think Cornyn would be all-in to stop him from turning Texas blue. Nope. Instead, he's trashing Paxton as lazy and a poor campaigner, while telling reporters the party shouldn't spend another dime on his race because of limited resources. That's rich. **Even worse, Cornyn is working with former President George W. Bush to pull money out of Texas to fund moderate Senate candidates in other states — many of whom are far bigger underdogs than Paxton.** With friends like these, who needs enemies?

body:
Trump is already trying to build the case to throw out the 2026 count in majority-Black cities and districts. | |

Peter, **** In February, Donald Trump named Philadelphia, Detroit, and Atlanta from the Oval Office, called their elections horrible corruption, and said federal agents should count the votes. This is part of Trump’s attempt to tell the American people that their votes should not count. **Trump is attacking majority-Black cities and districts whose ballots decide statewide races. He is building the case to treat the November 3 count as illegitimate, even as his approval ratings continue to plummet.** Right now Trump’s Justice Department is suing states, including Pennsylvania, for their voter rolls. He is trying to delegitimize the vote, claiming voter fraud where there is none, and baselessly demonizing vote-by-mail, even as he votes by mail himself. **All of this is setting the stage for election denial claims when he and his MAGA minions don't like the results.** **Fortune 500 CEOs employ millions of people in those same cities and districts that Trump is demonizing. These corporations write the political checks, buy the ads, and get lawmakers on the phone.** After 2020, in the midst of Trump’s election denial, too many CEOs waited while voters in majority-Black cities and districts were told their ballots were the problem. **Their silence only emboldens Trump’s lies.** **Fortune 500 CEOs need to take the Hands Off Our Vote pledge.** We need them to speak out **publicly right now, opposing election interference and sabotage, standing for democracy and insisting** that every eligible vote must be counted. And we need them to speak out again _after_ Election Day and say the election reflects the will of the people, the results must be certified, and that elected officials must be seated. | | | Can I level with you?
When I was growing up in Peoria, my family didn't have much. But we had something that mattered more than money: The belief that if you worked hard enough, this country would meet you halfway. That the doors would open. That the next generation would have it better than the last.
I built my entire life around that belief.
But I look around today and I'm concerned. Not for myself — for the families who are where my family was. The ones working two jobs and still falling behind. The kids graduating into mountains of debt. The parents who are doing everything right and still can't afford to keep a roof over their heads.
The American Dream that saved my family is slipping out of reach for millions of people just like us. And I refuse to accept that as inevitable.

That's exactly why I started Equal Opportunity Now.
**[Because I genuinely believe that if we don't fight like hell right now — to elect leaders who give a damn, to take on the powerful interests rigging the system against working families, to build something that lasts beyond this moment — we are going to lose something we can never get back.](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140090567/649491273/1090555623?amount=25&refcode=260927_eoq&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQMDUvMS83MzE2OSIsDQogICJEaXN0cmlidXRpb25VbmlxdWVJZCI6ICJhODMxNDMxMS1hMGJhLWYxMTEtYTZhOS0wMDBkM2E1NmQyZjciLA0KICAiRW1haWxBZGRyZXNzIjogImRwd2lsbGlzNjdAZ21haWwuY29tIg0KfQ%3D%3D&hmac=qFGIeeiMhpinFQA2UJLW-h4m4rbLcyiXTpkp1xACYuI=)**

Our campaign is required by the FEC (Federal Election Commission) to compile a report of every dollar we raised and spent each quarter. The FEC then publishes the report on its website, which is available to anyone who wants to read it.

The third-quarter fundraising period closes at midnight on Wednesday, September 30th. Once we’ve closed our books, my finance team will submit the official report for publication in October.

The FEC finance report is proof of our commitment to rejecting corporate PAC money. It also influences race ratings, shapes media coverage, and lets our opponents know exactly where we sit.

subject: He knows he failed Texans
body:
Say it to my face, Greg Abbott.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter, Greg Abbott continues to repeatedly attack me with false claims.
But the difference between Greg Abbott and me is that I’m willing to defend my plan for the future of Texas in a head-to-head debate — _and he isn’t_.
Abbott’s decade-long record speaks for itself.
Texans have faced years of rising costs, some of the highest uninsured rates in the country, families are struggling to keep the lights on because electricity has become so expensive, and billions of our taxpayer dollars flowing to politically connected donors and special interests instead of working people.
Greg Abbott has sold out the people of Texas to the highest bidder, and he’s dodging accountability by refusing to face me in front of voters.
I’ve made it clear that I’m ready to debate Greg Abbott — but he’s stayed silent. He’s silent because he knows he’s failed Texans.

body:
Data centers are costing Texas.

| | [](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140091018/649492918/-463234460?refcode=emailheader&refcode2=448f926b-a3ba-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ms=260927_kh_data&nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9OR1AvTkdQNjEvMS8xMTA5NjQiLA0KICAiRGlzdHJpYnV0aW9uVW5pcXVlSWQiOiAiNDQ4ZjkyNmItYTNiYS1mMTExLWE2YTktMDAwZDNhNTZkMmY3IiwNCiAgIkVtYWlsQWRkcmVzcyI6ICJkcHdpbGxpczY3QGdtYWlsLmNvbSINCn0%3D&hmac=mQdNb3cJzRraRasaAC__9dkOvdRJLAp5O5bIyar-NGo=)

Friend, A new report found that Texas data centers already used an estimated 25 billion gallons of water in 2025 alone, with projections showing that number could balloon to easily clear 100 billion gallons a year by 2030. Researchers estimate that Texas data centers and the natural gas power plants being built to serve them could use a combined 9% of the state’s water by 2040. We've got 70 of these facilities built or planned nearby, and almost no oversight over what they're taking from our communities to power an AI boom most of us never asked for. Some of these facilities are being built on 500-plus-acre footprints, carved right out of Texas land—straining water supplies that farmers, ranchers, and families in our district already depend on. My opponent is part of a Texas Republican political network that Elon Musk, one of the biggest players in the AI industry, has spent heavily to prop up. When the same industry pillaging our water and land is also bankrolling the politicians who are supposed to regulate it, you can guess how that usually goes. I won't let data centers pillage our land and resources without a fight. As a scientist, I believe sustainable growth and innovation are possible, but not at the expense of the water our community needs to survive. **[We have our last end-of-quarter reporting deadline approaching in just a few days. clean_body: Data centers are costing Texas. | | = Friend, A new report found that Texas data centers already used an estimated 25 billion gallons of water in 2025 alone, with projections showing that number could balloon to easily clear 100 billion gallons a year by 2030. Researchers estimate that Texas data centers and the natural gas power plants being built to serve them could use a combined 9% of the state’s water by 2040. We've got 70 of these facilities built or planned nearby, and almost no oversight over what they're taking from our communities to power an AI boom most of us never asked for. Some of these facilities are being built on 500-plus-acre footprints, carved right out of Texas land—straining water supplies that farmers, ranchers, and families in our district already depend on. My opponent is part of a Texas Republican political network that Elon Musk, one of the biggest players in the AI industry, has spent heavily to prop up. When the same industry pillaging our water and land is also bankrolling the politicians who are supposed to regulate it, you can guess how that usually goes. I won't let data centers pillage our land and resources without a fight. As a scientist, I believe sustainable growth and innovation are possible, but not at the expense of the water our community needs to survive. = | = | = ---|--- = | = = | = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your secure donation will go through immediately. Dear Friend,

C.S. Lewis is one of my favorite authors, full stop.

His writings were essential in deepening my faith in God and my understanding of the Bible. Maybe, since you opened my email, he has helped you, too.

Why are Lewis's words so powerful?

It's because he was a master at addressing life's most important questions. His vivid language is delightful and captivating to read.

Lewis's signature ability to communicate the truth about Christianity has inspired so many skeptics to **become** believers and even more Christians to renew and deepen their faith. He is certainly the greatest Christian apologist of the twentieth century.

To help you learn more about Lewis's works related to Christianity, we produced a powerful, free course, "**C.S. Lewis on Christianity** ," which you can now own on DVD absolutely free.

**Claim your FREE DVD set of "C.S. Lewis on Christianity" using this secure link:**

[https://info.hillsdale.edu/free-cs-lewis-christianity-dvd](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/2aH-Ytn4okVKyJ9RNMAVfAgVX-hjBFLfQCU9xjd-6T2Gd6pk9v8KKxahSKNFQ74SFHhlpNURrxDWB7CB5-2y9vwgCB2_kIUPrGFpwtwFJmiFVMirgDCs0es0f8EdpDSvEZqDDK6QACVVZSWVauf1dmYyEBv_tDT_hmzea80NjTrfNl-P7ynHupbz9fLZ6gBlQhw_95vJXIcf4t5IdtA2usdcwmgPkLnYYkarYwLZ0eGTf5h2oSNZhrEOZIPU6dhsz4p-0XFUzRQszAZ4QBLyYsOTyu4TenLigZwMoSXM3cZsLeEOUMZiP8ih2ryf65u1fEcmKB3AWDoiiEQun4Xi2pRg8nflchb-WaT7uVr-4Dmqvts2FMvBbaXnEEGDhGZahR7WH0hva1DiXmOp094ZvWzdACgPbHRWAkIVaG0tYGkiR_pibqdtEASv_4SBjQO6cZCUzDWRZ_cAh48Nz1HwOknSo1v2BSL_fVAqLnXpMlFVZUY9TGWjJrDhJh_EsCzOSDoCeHZVcX0Meye_AQlDkQFP5jR7rIM_Eb7MM2OR5BUbiviHV-IzCETqkzWPlIealLkTJ4QeSp0rl1tl6tOA4M4X-3r--himq4HJmqf9xilMdU-vQg5fIasuFbQc1uyEA3Z0SGtPdkGQCP7i1dhJIj_Rflgx3dUbuxHyF4cDW3FzYZPwaNQYOqBk1SkVbya6S3JNuCKBPs4_RX2wRn1v64RwNhHxxBHrRym0qX224rfWGXnyp2MorMG5YwvmCe9RrD9QsYx-9-CFywM/Ru3eLQzeLj5_gp8EdMevIIV9wWw98JIr/25)

In this course, you will study Lewis's profound insights on the central topics of Christianity, including:
* Good and evil
* Conversion and faith
* Prayer and the Bible
* Suffering and death
* Heaven and Hell

The instructor, Michael Ward, is a distinguished visiting professor at Hillsdale College and a member of the Faculty of Theology and Religion at the University of Oxford. He wrote _Planet Narnia: The Seven Heavens in the Imagination of C.S. Lewis_ and _After Humanity: A Guide to C.S. Lewis 's The Abolition of Man_. He even spent three years living in Lewis's Oxford home as the resident Warden of The Kilns!

You'll find this course especially moving because it examines C.S. Lewis's beautiful writings about faith. You'll even trace Lewis's own journey from skeptic to believer. The combination provides an opportunity for you to grow in your knowledge and understanding of Christianity.

[So please join us in studying Christianity with C.S. Lewis and Michael Ward with this beautiful free DVD set.](http://links.newsletter.conservativedirect.com/s/c/X5AfnnfxxpfpupxNG4jU2kQ5DCIUH5RIRNS-uqyMiApwIHCZSRddTgXWpuhHJ7hxuFTTQzRSRr9gKbV5e66wWQRWC8DsTCelyDqyaKZYL2u9KNxB9vRrk1r9I3A-mJNqJlXFC5UizOZtQGnQ6Zrhcy0QxhU-cXv3S3dMgR9vbvzQygqJ8g4f5SIiv75EqwYjMACn887I50jza9rjlw3i0aXDzRxWymf5vTHw9hxIUXQYiri5EMZXXdOiJU519cMCmaqg-YIRGjyDf9aoO9mQZ0gGDw9CTJFQC9LffjhQ6SoDsBm2e9hkFLnltmikqCqgemTF4Xtrih7H5aaQ9Wgney1wCS1aLXjckHEoD3ovIshon-wUe8xbVUbGvpLR6WZzk7YtSp3j8jyL_PpUN74GBbBGsg45X2w6Iy6oTRyOWlECj_AiNcAC7PkJvnmCql7qZXwS_AxBiCBvmsdFsK1l7EI6AlxKR2MFGxvNqCTsGySDlaTCSeMSMS6C7E4wit1nc32Ee30_qk0lax_mkf0YSMm9T9Xoe-wrM2DSz5eeSwkkI3XgIMNV6BJG43Zs9vTrZJGogjHBcJTcQRy-rSbpHamUxNtOJW3cCXNTRShDeBCfpR4HfjN7OS5c_BP1qSlPPe0wz3dZibeKt3TxHyd65MuKBllj8ItQqsDmj5R2yS70e6SYL9oQGbYmwWYgljvllVPGA6gWAvVgzE3vuv0zA9-DojCC_0Oaj-6I8oDTHcOu-Da2GY9KphpV6HTmTIqFhWWEVRfyTjYOWK0/2vpeMkLyG1UkKat-rDsDzgvWvi8jewp6/25)

**Team:** President Donald Trump has repeatedly slapped sweeping tariffs on foreign imports. Nearly every time, the stock market reacted with major losses, including the biggest one-day drop since the pandemic flattened the global economy. Many economists have said these tariffs are much worse than expected, and investors have dumped shares in companies they predict will suffer most from what is effectively a business tax. **In many cases that tax will be passed on to consumers.** “ _This is a game changer, not only for the U.S. economy but for the global economy,_ ” Olu Sonola, Fitch Ratings’ head of U.S. Economic Research, said in a report. “ _Many countries will likely end up in a recession._ ” We would like to hear from more voters in your area on this issue. As I write this email, one thing keeps going through my mind: **It 's now or never.**
**The final FEC end-of-quarter deadline is just three days away, and we 've set an ambitious $1 million goal.** That's what it will take to stand up to Roger Marshall and the super PACs supporting him. They've already poured millions into this race to flood the airwaves with attack ads against me. We _must_ hit our goal to have the resources to fight back.
What we raise by Sept. 30 will be a matter of public record, and everyone -- from Roger Marshall to his corporate PAC allies, the media and even our own supporters -- will be watching closely to see whether we fall short. If we do, Marshall's allies will take it as a sign of weakness, and they'll increase their spending and attack ads accordingly.
Our momentum over the past few months has been incredible. Multiple polls have shown me leading Roger Marshall, including a recent poll that has me up by 2 points. Election experts at Real Clear Polling just shifted this race to "Toss Up" status. And the New York Times called this one of the most competitive races in the country.
**This surge of support is all because of amazing supporters like you. It 's thanks to people like you that we had early fundraising success that helped us meet with Kansans across the state, spread our unifying message and draw national attention to this race. It's because of dedicated people like you that we have a narrow lead and have a real chance to win in November.**
But now, with the final FEC quarterly deadline before the election just around the corner, we have to prove to Marshall, his allies and everyone watching that our momentum is still going strong. We have to show them, in no uncertain terms, that we are prepared to meet this moment and respond to whatever they throw at us.
**That 's why hitting our $1 million end-of-quarter goal is so crucial. We only have until midnight on Sept. 30 to prove that our grassroots movement has what it takes to win. I know from listening to Kansans all across the state that they're sick and tired of Roger Marshall letting them down over and over again.**
**[It's now or never. Please, will you give anything you can spare to help us hit this all-important goal and make sure we have what it takes to send Roger Marshall packing in November? At this critical time, every dollar makes a difference.](https://link.sbstck.com/redirect/ee588d06-d073-4989-97d2-c4a199f17b8a?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)**
With your support -- and the support of thousands of people like you -- we can do this.
Thank you,
Adam
