Peter, Washington has spent my entire adult life treating the word "socialist" like it's something dangerous.
Republicans put it on cable chyrons, corporate Democrats run from it, and both parties assume voters will recoil.
But this year, things are changing.
New polls show more and more voters - especially independents - are seeing that socialism is actually the path to a better future.
But polls are only one scoreboard, and I want to win on every one they can check.
For us, the next one comes Wednesday at midnight, when our books close for the quarter.
For decades, the billionaire class has decided who gets taken seriously in Washington, and they've happily spent whatever it took to keep socialists off the list. Our FEC report will show a union worker running without a dime of corporate PAC money, funded by working people who've stopped waiting for the wealthy to share power and started organizing to take it.
[If you can, contribute before Wednesday at midnight to help us hit our goal and put another W on the board for socialism.](https://irrem7hbb.cc.rs6.net/tn.jsp?f=001DCBOzgG5y4nSvovZ-TCFPlhd70cFt2V7Q2khFgOfQSYQerU4zrDo_ijHVipjTRB3OCX13r7BG9mc95gtY4TBq8LzUicds45iBDse8loVLfHFeevYKvkX1yvPVVtUIM7fGolDW-RDekWJ21vfSwr8lVE5LGk5OOTWkQOANAS5vK8DkHNTGgOubBh7ZDN5VxjFcmPffB-jOIvAys1oX0XmOFSDkJ5YrLyvgGaoL36z6Z-Rb8M_5fx2ZhWXAEMY3jid&c=tS0A8noDry6BpUHnOmPpE8VlNFDX3R9Mt5dOKH0vv0VrSF17KJD7tA==&ch=6srvXzVju9rASk89bisB8CHz8ULvwLYXW-6GLPbcsEbisANAym0pWg==)

body:
A note before the month ends

| |

Peter, We're closing in on the end of the month, and I wanted to write to you before the deadline hits. Every seat matters this November. Every congressional race, every state legislative campaign, every school board contest is a chance to push back against a Republican Party that can't be trusted with the economy, with our democracy, or with the basic rights of Virginia families. And every month between now and the election is a month that separates campaigns that build the infrastructure to win from ones that don't. I've spent this month doing the work, through town halls, community sit-downs across HD-28, and fighting for the affordability agenda But I can't keep it going without you. Iran Says It Won't Back Down. Washington Isn't Offering an Alternative.
Trump called Iran's rejected Hormuz plan a losing hand; Araghchi and Pezeshkian pushed back hard, but Tehran is still routing its response through mediators rather than walking away. Markets reopen Monday into the same unresolved standoff.
|
---
The weekend produced the direct exchange this newsletter flagged Saturday as the open question: how Tehran would respond to Trump's rejection of its seven-day Hormuz plan. **Verified fact:** Trump said Iran's proposal “would not be acceptable,” adding Iran only wants a deal “because they are losing so badly.” **Verified fact:** Foreign Minister Araghchi responded that Iran “will not back down” on its conditions and called Trump's statements historically “contradictory,” while President Pezeshkian said Tehran “no longer trusted” negotiations with Washington, citing a pattern of strikes and sanctions following prior talks. **Verified fact:** Iran is now awaiting a response through mediators rather than engaging Trump's public rejection directly, and no alternative U.S. proposal has been offered. Markets were closed for the weekend after Friday's session, which closed the week higher on equities even as the 10-year Treasury yield hit 5.18%, its highest since the 2008 financial crisis.
| | Regime Signal 01 — Both Sides Escalated Rhetoric While Leaving the Diplomatic Door Open
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump's “losing so badly” framing and Pezeshkian's “no longer trusted” statement are both notably harder rhetoric than either side used last week, yet Iran is still routing its response through mediators rather than walking away from the table. **Our interpretation:** this is a pattern this newsletter has seen before in this conflict — public rhetoric hardening even as the private, procedural channel (mediated responses, not a formal walkout) stays open. **What remains unknown** is whether Pezeshkian's “no longer trusted” comment reflects an actual shift in Tehran's negotiating posture or is domestic-audience messaging layered on top of an otherwise unchanged mediated process.
| | Regime Signal 02 — Trump's Framing Suggests No Urgency to Counter-Offer
---|---
**Verified fact:** as of this writing, Washington has not put forward an alternative proposal, and Trump's public comments suggest satisfaction with the current military and sanctions posture rather than pressure to negotiate further. **Our interpretation:** a rejection paired with no counter-offer and a stated view that Iran is “losing so badly” reads as Washington judging that time and battlefield pressure favor the U.S. position — consistent with Friday's reported aide comments about a bombing campaign timed to the midterms rather than to Iranian concessions.
| | Regime Signal 03 — The Market Reopens Monday Into an Unresolved Standoff and a Fifth Potential Yield Session
---|---
**Verified fact:** Friday's close left the 10-year yield at a fresh multi-decade high for a fourth consecutive session, with no scheduled catalyst over the weekend to interrupt that trend before Monday's open. **Our interpretation:** the weekend's rhetorical escalation on Iran, absent any concrete military or economic action, is unlikely by itself to be the catalyst that breaks the yield curve's recent pattern of climbing independent of headline news.
| | This Week’s Confirmation Point
---|---
Whether Monday's reopen extends the Treasury yield's climb to a fifth consecutive session, and whether Iran's mediator-channel response over the coming days narrows the sequencing dispute or simply restates it in Pezeshkian's harder rhetorical terms.

Policy Transmission — September 27, 2026
The Rhetoric Hardened. The Actual Negotiating Channel May Not Have.
Trump and Iran's leadership traded their sharpest public language yet over the rejected Hormuz plan — but Tehran is still working through mediators, and Washington still hasn't offered an alternative. The gap between the public and private tracks is this week's real signal.
|
---
| | The Mechanism
---|---
This newsletter tracked Friday's rejection of Iran's Hormuz plan as the expected outcome of an unresolved sequencing dispute. The weekend's transmission channel is rhetorical: how each side chose to characterize that rejection publicly, which shapes the negotiating room available to both governments going forward.
| | What Was Actually Said
---|---
**Verified fact:** Trump said Iran's proposal “would not be acceptable” and that Iran wants a deal only “because they are losing so badly.” **Verified fact:** Araghchi said Iran “will not back down” and called Trump's statements historically “contradictory”; Pezeshkian said Tehran “no longer trusted” negotiations with Washington, pointing to a pattern of strikes and sanctions following past talks. **Reported claim:** Iran is awaiting a formal response through mediators rather than engaging Trump's comments directly, and no U.S. counter-proposal has surfaced.
| | Regime Classification: PRESSURE, With Both Governments Now Playing to Domestic Audiences
---|---
**Our interpretation:** Pezeshkian's “no longer trusted” language and Trump's “losing so badly” framing both read as messaging calibrated for domestic political consumption — a midterms-conscious U.S. audience and an Iranian public asked to accept continued hardship — more than as literal descriptions of the mediated channel's status. **What remains unknown** is whether this rhetorical hardening is contained to public statements while private, mediator-run diplomacy continues largely unchanged, or whether it foreshadows an actual narrowing of Tehran's willingness to negotiate.
| | Why the Absence of a US Counter-Offer Is the More Important Signal
---|---
Rhetoric from both sides was, on some level, predictable given the domestic pressures each leader faces. **Next confirmation point:** whether Washington puts forward any counter-proposal in the coming days, versus continuing to let the current sanctions-and-blockade posture stand as its de facto position while awaiting the midterms.

The weekend's transmission channel is rhetorical: how each side chose to characterize that rejection publicly, which shapes the negotiating room available to both governments going forward. | | What Was Actually Said ---|--- Verified fact: Trump said Iran's proposal “would not be acceptable” and that Iran wants a deal only “because they are losing so badly.” Verified fact: Araghchi said Iran “will not back down” and called Trump's statements historically “contradictory”; Pezeshkian said Tehran “no longer trusted” negotiations with Washington, pointing to a pattern of strikes and sanctions following past talks. Reported claim: Iran is awaiting a formal response through mediators rather than engaging Trump's comments directly, and no U.S. counter-proposal has surfaced. | | Regime Classification: PRESSURE, With Both Governments Now Playing to Domestic Audiences ---|--- Our interpretation: Pezeshkian's “no longer trusted” language and Trump's “losing so badly” framing both read as messaging calibrated for domestic political consumption — a midterms-conscious U.S. audience and an Iranian public asked to accept continued hardship — more than as literal descriptions of the mediated channel's status. What remains unknown is whether this rhetorical hardening is contained to public statements while private, mediator-run diplomacy continues largely unchanged, or whether it foreshadows an actual narrowing of Tehran's willingness to negotiate. | | Why the Absence of a US Counter-Offer Is the More Important Signal ---|--- Rhetoric from both sides was, on some level, predictable given the domestic pressures each leader faces. Next confirmation point: whether Washington puts forward any counter-proposal in the coming days, versus continuing to let the current sanctions-and-blockade posture stand as its de facto position while awaiting the midterms. | | | (ad by Behind the Markets) | | | At Deep Regime Trends, we write for people who think for themselves. disclaimer_text: Paid for by Alexandria Ocasio-Cortez for Congress
body:
#
We’re in Ithaca with Alexandria today and she wants you to be the first to see our new palm cards to turn out inactive voters:
Inactive voters are voters in New York State who haven’t voted in two consecutive federal elections and are at risk of being purged from the voter rolls. And once a voter is purged, they have to re-register to vote to cast a ballot.
**We’re printing tens of thousands of these palm cards, in English and Spanish, to reach as many people as we can to tell them how they can reactivate their voter status.**
Our organizers and volunteers will be putting these directly into the hands of voters across New York State, reaching folks who have sat out recent elections.
The stakes this fall are too high to leave anyone on the sidelines.
Talking with voters face to face is how this campaign has always organized, and it's how we'll reach communities that are too often overlooked or taken for granted.

But winning means making sure voters know the truth about Marie Gluesenkamp Perez and her record.Marie has spent years cultivating an image as an independent-minded moderate. But when you look at her actual voting record in Congress, she still votes with the hard left of her party, over and over again.That’s a record voters deserve to know.Over these final weeks, we need the resources to cut through the millions being spent on advertising, communicate directly with voters across Southwest Washington, and make sure they have the facts before they cast their ballots.That’s why this fundraising deadline matters so much.We have just three days left in the quarter. This race is winnable. ##### _This piece by Jonathan Larsen originally ran in_ [The Fucking News](https://substack.com/redirect/06af0610-ae9e-4672-9207-2584bf5f4328?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) _on 9/23/26. It is republished here with his permission. Vance 's announcement took place on Tuesday, Sept. 22._
_**Cliff 's Note:**_
##### Vance and Oz threw 750,000 people off their health insurance this week and called it fighting fraud. Then they held up one case as proof of how bad things got under Biden.
##### Jonathan Larsen, one of the sharpest writers in independent media, did what the D.C. press corps didn't: he pulled the court filings. What he found behind the paywall flips their story on its head, and you'll want it in your pocket the next time someone tells you this is about "fraud."
##### [This is what $60 a year buys: receipts, not talking points, from people who actually read the documents. Subscribe to Blue Amp Media and read the whole thing](https://substack.com/redirect/65720257-aa78-4b0c-b15d-7afb1d3fa66b?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
_**-- Cliff**_

* * *
_**by Jonathan Larsen**_
Vice President **JD Vance** on Tuesday [announced](https://substack.com/redirect/43eb1f3e-1a08-435a-90c9-5849365f62b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) the removal of 750,000 people from the federal health insurance program known as Obamacare.
Vance made the announcement alongside Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator **Mehmet Oz** as part of an accelerating get-out-the-vote operation on behalf of Democrats.
Stripping health insurance from almost a million people in one live-streamed campaign rally was just the latest Republican effort to encourage Democratic voter turnout, along with distributing flyers across Iran, fundraising with tariffs that raise funds from consumers, and door-knocking operations such as knocking down the doors of the East Wing of the White House.
Vance and Oz were roundly ridiculed for the incoherence of their announcement, which included the prospect of kicking another 419,000 people off Obamacare, all on the premise of fraud.
The main problem cited was that Vance and Oz said they were removing people from Obamacare who had not, records showed, filed any claims. This was shared as evidence that these people don't really exist.
In reality, people who don't file claims are the lifeblood of insuring people so they can keep their life and blood. Insurance _insures_ people against the _possibility_ that they might have to file a claim. Insurance can afford to pay out claims _because_ most people don't make them.
Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.x0ofl75yqOXyLjmh0xok-9iiAf7g7HrYqUMHM3xWiT8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget-preamble&utm_content=217723845)
In the case of health care, one would think _everyone_ would file a claim for regular checkups but ... and bear with me now ... what if some people can't even afford those in the Trumpconomy?
"This is not about cutting off anybody from their benefits. It's about cutting off fraudsters from stealing from these programs," Vance said while cutting people off from their benefits.
The cuts will save an estimated $2.2 billion, Vance said without saying how one saves money by cutting off people who are paying monthly premiums but not filing claims.
"[T]hose 750,000 people are people that ... either don't know that they're enrolled in the program, aren't using the program at all, are unaware of it or ... are potentially phantom people who are enrolled against their will, or maybe they don't even exist," Vance explained without explaining how phantoms can rip off a program they don't know they're in because they don't exist.
As The Hill [notes](https://substack.com/redirect/43eb1f3e-1a08-435a-90c9-5849365f62b0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), Vance's campaign rally comes after Republicans have already boosted Democratic turnout by turning out millions of people from Obamacare by allowing tax subsidies to expire.
Vance blamed Pres. **Joe Biden** for letting too many people get health insurance without doing enough to stop fraud. (Unlike Pres. **Donald Trump** who is ending illegal fraud by [making fraud legal](https://substack.com/redirect/c6d2b0b2-22b5-42f8-a51c-fd69fde37f77?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).)
After a dramatic Obamacare expansion during COVID, the Biden administration decertified about 200 brokers -- who get commissions for signing people up for Obamacare -- for juking the system. Trump recertified them because nothing counts til he does it, and then decertified more.
Vance's fraud task force -- meaning, a task force that is a fraud -- has [denied](https://substack.com/redirect/202e8ebc-b793-49cb-b3ad-991e4174d7c0?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) billions in Medicaid funds to states that allegedly don't do enough to fight fraud. Medicaid is the health plan people can apply for if they're too poor for Obamacare. Unless they're kicked off both.
[Upgrade to paid](https://substack.com/redirect/2/eyJlIjoiaHR0cHM6Ly93d3cuYmx1ZWFtcC5jby9zdWJzY3JpYmU_.x0ofl75yqOXyLjmh0xok-9iiAf7g7HrYqUMHM3xWiT8?&utm_medium=email&utm_source=subscribe-widget&utm_content=217723845)
Vance has targeted California and Minnesota as not fighting fraud. Which nicely teed up Tuesday's example of fraud: From Florida.
Oz spotlighted the case of two Obamacare brokers, **Cory Lloyd** and **Steven Strong** , as examples of the Biden-era fraud that Trump alone can fix. Because **I** couldn't find sufficient details on the case in Tuesday's reporting, I went down the rabbit hole, which I have the luxury of doing thanks to your support.
**Newsfuckers** , here's what I found, digging through legal documents, about these Biden-era fraudsters...

Cliff 's Note: Vance and Oz threw 750,000 people off their health insurance this week and called it fighting fraud. Then they held up one case as proof of how bad things got under Biden. Jonathan Larsen, one of the sharpest writers in independent media, did what the D.C. press corps didn't: he pulled the court filings. What he found behind the paywall flips their story on its head, and you'll want it in your pocket the next time someone tells you this is about "fraud." . -- Cliff by Jonathan Larsen Vice President JD Vance on Tuesday the removal of 750,000 people from the federal health insurance program known as Obamacare. Vance made the announcement alongside Centers for Medicare and Medicaid Services (CMS) Administrator Mehmet Oz as part of an accelerating get-out-the-vote operation on behalf of Democrats. Stripping health insurance from almost a million people in one live-streamed campaign rally was just the latest Republican effort to encourage Democratic voter turnout, along with distributing flyers across Iran, fundraising with tariffs that raise funds from consumers, and door-knocking operations such as knocking down the doors of the East Wing of the White House. Vance and Oz were roundly ridiculed for the incoherence of their announcement, which included the prospect of kicking another 419,000 people off Obamacare, all on the premise of fraud. The main problem cited was that Vance and Oz said they were removing people from Obamacare who had not, records showed, filed any claims. This was shared as evidence that these people don't really exist. In reality, people who don't file claims are the lifeblood of insuring people so they can keep their life and blood. Insurance insures people against the possibility that they might have to file a claim. Insurance can afford to pay out claims because most people don't make them. Blue Amp Media is a reader-supported publication. To receive new posts and support our work, consider becoming a free or paid subscriber. In the case of health care, one would think everyone would file a claim for regular checkups but ... and bear with me now ... what if some people can't even afford those in the Trumpconomy? "This is not about cutting off anybody from their benefits. It's about cutting off fraudsters from stealing from these programs," Vance said while cutting people off from their benefits. The cuts will save an estimated $2.2 billion, Vance said without saying how one saves money by cutting off people who are paying monthly premiums but not filing claims. "[T]hose 750,000 people are people that ... either don't know that they're enrolled in the program, aren't using the program at all, are unaware of it or ... are potentially phantom people who are enrolled against their will, or maybe they don't even exist," Vance explained without explaining how phantoms can rip off a program they don't know they're in because they don't exist. As The Hill , Vance's campaign rally comes after Republicans have already boosted Democratic turnout by turning out millions of people from Obamacare by allowing tax subsidies to expire. Vance blamed Pres. Joe Biden for letting too many people get health insurance without doing enough to stop fraud. (Unlike Pres. Donald Trump who is ending illegal fraud by .) After a dramatic Obamacare expansion during COVID, the Biden administration decertified about 200 brokers -- who get commissions for signing people up for Obamacare -- for juking the system. Trump recertified them because nothing counts til he does it, and then decertified more. Vance's fraud task force -- meaning, a task force that is a fraud -- has billions in Medicaid funds to states that allegedly don't do enough to fight fraud. Medicaid is the health plan people can apply for if they're too poor for Obamacare. Unless they're kicked off both. Vance has targeted California and Minnesota as not fighting fraud. Which nicely teed up Tuesday's example of fraud: From Florida. Oz spotlighted the case of two Obamacare brokers, Cory Lloyd and Steven Strong , as examples of the Biden-era fraud that Trump alone can fix. Because I couldn't find sufficient details on the case in Tuesday's reporting, I went down the rabbit hole, which I have the luxury of doing thanks to your support. subject: Abbott has never done this before, Peter.
body:
Two rating shifts in a month, and Abbott just placed his first negative ad buy of the race. He’s scared.
# [](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)[](https://ginafortexas.com/?refcode=em_ms_gh_header)
Peter,
In the same 24 hours that Fox News moved the Texas governor’s race even further away from him, Greg Abbott did something he’s never done before in this race: he went negative on TV.
**Abbott recently launched a $12 MILLION attack ad buy against me — his first negative spending of the entire campaign.**
Let’s be clear about why this is happening. Fox News has now moved this race in our direction twice in a month, from Solid Republican to Likely Republican in August and from Likely Republican to Lean Republican today. Abbott even reversed course on his own data center policy this week as the pressure mounted.
**_Now he’s panic-spending millions on attack ads._**
Abbott wouldn’t spend $12 million on negative attack ads against a candidate he thought he was beating easily. He’s opening his firehose of money to drown us out because he’s scared.
We knew the attacks were coming. What we need is the resources to answer them, get our message in front of Texas voters, and keep our momentum going for the next six weeks until November 3.

clean_body: A glitch on Facebook just lost us thousands and thousands of dollars | | | = Hi, we just had a major setback at the worst possible time. Half of our Facebook ads went down this weekend, which means most grassroots supporters weren’t able to make contributions on that platform for 48 hours. We still don’t know why this happened, but we do know most of our ads are still dark – and we don’t have any time to waste. This couldn’t have come at a worse time. Crypto and data center billionaires are launching a $30 million ad blitz, Donald Trump just poured in another $5 million on Friday night, and we’re chasing down our biggest public reporting deadline of the election on Wednesday. We needed to raise $75,000 from these online ads over the weekend, and now we’re WAY behind. We might not even be able to afford our next set of TV ads or voter outreach. = If you've saved payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | = Thanks to the dark-money groups and billionaires like Peter Thiel and Elon Musk, Republicans are outspending us by as much as 7:1 every single day. And there’s no way to sugarcoat it: If we keep getting drowned out, we will lose this race and our path to Senate control. Experts are saying Ohio could be the seat that secures Democrats a majority in the Senate, and The Washington Post just said we are the #2 state most likely to flip blue. We’re counting on ads like these on Facebook to meet our fundraising goals, but we just lost a TON of money due to this technical glitch. = | | = Thank you for reading on a Sunday, Sherrod | | Note: This email only reflects donations made online with this email address. If you've made a previous contribution via check or with a different email address/phone number, you may not see it here – but know that Sherrod and our entire team are deeply grateful for your support. = Hey there! It's Sherrod Brown. There's nobody fighting for Ohioans in the U.S. Senate right now, and I won't sit on the sidelines while working people get screwed over by large corporations and wealthy political donors. If you work hard, you should be able to afford a decent life. But the reality is, life is too expensive. Costs are going up. Wages are staying stagnant. Working people are working harder than ever before, and they're not getting their share of the profit. This campaign is all about changing that – and election analysts say we have a strong shot at winning in November. But I'll need your help to pull it off: My opponent is a Washington insider being propped up by the Republican establishment, and he's got virtually unlimited resources. That's not how our campaign works. We're a grassroots movement, and that means we rely on ordinary people chipping in a couple bucks. = If you'd like to receive exclusive updates from my team, you can text "OHIO" to 64054. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1001&akid=3312%2E251025%2EHm_Dcf ]Abdul for US Senate [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/1219?t=1002&akid=3312%2E251025%2EHm_Dcf ]Abdul for US Senate

Hey Peter,

You've probably seen by now that MAGA Republicans like to use my full name
in their attacks: Abdulrahman Mohamed El-Sayed.

Donald Trump uses it as if it’s a punchline. ̄\_(ツ)_/ ̄

Peter, I’ve spent
the majority of my career being someone who’s relatively young, relatively
brown, and relatively Muslim. Something I’ve learned along the way is that
when someone reaches for your name instead of your record, it's because
your record is the thing they can't touch:

* I’ve helped make government agencies actually work for Michiganders —
first by rebuilding Detroit’s Health Department after bankruptcy, and
then restructuring Wayne County’s Department of Health, Human &
Veterans Services.
* As a public servant, I’ve removed lead from elementary schools, taken
on Michigan’s biggest polluters, and made life-saving Narcan
universally accessible.

There’s nothing for MAGA Republicans to attack there — so that’s why
they’re resorting to a politics rooted in hatred instead.

Meanwhile, their guy, Mike Rogers, has a record he'd rather Michiganders
never look at too closely:

* Mike Rogers voted to raise his own pay in Congress.
* He championed a bill that helped create the opioid crisis.
* Then, after spending 15 years in Washington, he left and got $14
million richer working for the corporations he used to regulate and
moved to Florida.

That’s why Rogers needs $70+ million worth of help to have a chance at
beating us in November.

We’re never going to outraise $70+ million, but we don’t have to. We just
need folks like you to pitch in $10 to help us respond to
the MAGA attacks and get our message in front of as many Michiganders as
possible. If we do that, we will win. [ https://act.abdulformichigan.com/go/507?c0=em-ms-aes-20260927-4-ak.Jy4Erd&amount=10&refcode=em20260927-3312&t=1004&akid=3312%2E251025%2EHm_Dcf ]Can I count on your
support, Peter?

In solidarity,

Abdul

subject: I need you to read this, Peter.
body:
Read before you go to bed

| | | | | | PLEASE WAIT! **

name: Letitia James
subject: They want to silence us...

body:
This is our country, and I'll be damned if they ruin it.

This administration wants to exert its power over our great state —
bringing their routine of lawlessness, hatred, and intimidation right to
our front door.

They want to tear down everything we've built, target our most vulnerable
neighbors, and rule through fear and cruelty.

As long as I'm Attorney General of New York, I won't let them. Not now.
Not ever.

The justice system is one of the last lines of defense we have against
this administration’s cruel agenda. It stands between them and the
vulnerable people they're targeting — immigrants, communities of color,
working families, and anyone who dares to speak truth to power.

I’ve spent my entire career using the law as a sword and a shield. I've
used that sword against the NRA, predatory landlords, and the president
every time he’s abused his power. And I've used that shield to protect
tenants, immigrants, everyday New Yorkers, and anyone else who needed a
fighter in their corner.

That's exactly why the bad actors want this office in their pocket —
they're afraid of being held accountable for their corruption. They've
seen what happens when I take on the powerful, and they want me gone. They
want an Attorney General who will look the other way while they line their
pockets and trample on the rights of everyday people.

But I am not afraid of them. I never have been.

We can win this race and keep delivering justice in New York and across
the country. But we must be courageous. And we must be united.

* * *
Congresswoman Delia Ramirez (D-IL) announced her plan to eliminate the Department of Homeland Security in a deliberate effort to end immigration enforcement by getting rid of Immigration and Customs Enforcement and Customs and Border Protection.
Ramirez explained her bill, The Reimagining Safety Act, is necessary because "DHS must be dismantled, piece by piece, and something new - a system that honors our rights, our dignity, and our humanity - must be built" and the bill "will dismantle DHS and create a new human- and community-centered federal department: The Department of Community Safety to promote collective care and well-being."
During her press conference about the bill, Ramirez addressed the attendees in English and Spanish.
In the Spanish portion of her event, she said Congress must get rid of DHS so "our people will no longer have to live in fear of an unjust system" and so that immigration is not handled by an agency that likes to label immigrants as terrorists.
## WATCH:
[](https://substack.com/redirect/c13b3051-f6ca-456c-9c46-437361ac6c23?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)
Ramirez's comments outlining her plan drew the most backlash, especially the part where she referred to illegal immigrants as "our people" in Spanish.
That phrasing is no accident. Far-left types like Ramirez are a prime example as to how insane our political system has become. Beyond her crazy idea to get rid of DHS to end immigration enforcement, Ramirez's family history emphasizes the importance of having sound national policy.
Ramirez is, by her own admission, a "proud anchor baby" since her mother arrived in the United States when she was pregnant after leaving Guatemala. The Congresswoman infamously declared she is more proud to be a Guatemalan than an American last year during a far-left conference in Mexico City.
Any time she has a chance to profess loyalty, she does so to people who are not American. Even before this bill's announcement, Ramirez has hammered the absurd message of "DHS is still the single greatest threat to our communities."

Ramirez has also come to the defense of fellow Democrat LaMonica McIver, who is in a court battle after being caught on camera assaulting federal law enforcement outside of an ICE facility in New Jersey last year.
"Rep McIver did her job, conducted oversight, and protected her constituents and our communities. Today's decision from the Third Circuit is an attack on Congressional oversight. I stand with Rep McIver. We will continue to fight for our communities, defend our rights, and hold this authoritarian administration accountable. The fight is not over!" said Ramirez.
It should be no surprise that people like Ramirez have no love or loyalty to the United States and seek to undermine it from their positions of power. It is why the midterms are so important.
Democrats have made no attempt to hide their plans should they gain control of Congress. All of the real gains made by the Trump administration will grind to a halt because Democrats will be hard at work for their people, and it's not Americans.

Good morning,

We’re looking for volunteers to join Team Jude's **Adopt-A-Voter Postcard Project! **This is a simple and fun way to help Team Jude reach voters across Minnesota.

Volunteers will write short, personal notes reminding voters who have received—or will automatically receive—a ballot to **complete and return their ballot and vote for Tad Jude and the Republican team.
**
**Time matters!** The sooner we reach these voters, the sooner we can encourage them to complete and return their ballots. Sometimes, a friendly, personal reminder is all it takes to make sure a ballot doesn’t get set aside and forgotten.

The project is easy and can be done **individually, with friends and family, or as a group.** We’ve created a simple instruction sheet with everything you need, including step-by-step directions, suggested messages, and instructions for returning the completed postcards in the correct order.

And most importantly—**have fun with it!** Grab some friends, write some postcards, take some pictures, and help us reach voters throughout Minnesota.

Thank you for giving your time and energy to help Tad and our Republican team.

**We truly appreciate every volunteer and every postcard!
**
**Ready to help?**

Simply reply to this email, and a member of our Field Team will reach out to get you started!

Best,
**Team Jude**

Stay tuned!** Tad’s Field Team has **Voter Outreach Blitz Days** planned in communities across Minnesota. We hope you will help us get the vote out!

I’m one of the newest members of the EMILYs List board of directors, but EMILYs List has been part of my story for a long time. I’ve been on the receiving end of early support from this organization, and I’ve seen up close what it can do for a candidate who’s willing to run hard in a tough race. **Not great news for voters, Team** _:_ Just weeks before the pivotal midterm elections, **Texas election officials have discovered that an unknown number of voter registration applications have not been processed** due to an error by the Texas Department of Public Safety. According to an email sent to county officials and provided to Votebeat, DPS failed to send the applications, which were submitted by voters through its online driver’s license portal, to county voter registrars for processing. **This DPS portal is a major voter registration channel in Texas.** From 2020 through 2024, about 6 million Texans used it to register to vote, according to testimony DPS officials provided to state lawmakers in 2025. _Texas has more than 18 million registered voters._ This is where you come in -- if you live in Texas or know someone who does, we have voter tools that you can use. **[Verify your registration, find out where to vote, get election reminders, and register if someone hasn't yet](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140096980/649512255/1044253134?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjUyNGVmOTc2LWMwYmEtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZHTsuWRFhP0VfE8i9nN_646fEeKx64aFUjBYUEROWWQ=&emci=97af5186-a8ba-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=524ef976-c0ba-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=33603084)**. **Voters have until October 5** to update their registrations and can check their status with our tools, on the [**Texas Secretary of State’s website**](https://click.ngpvan.com/k/140096981/649512256/864965444?nvep=ew0KICAiVGVuYW50VXJpIjogIm5ncHZhbjovL3Zhbi9FQS9FQTAwNy8xLzg5MjE1IiwNCiAgIkRpc3RyaWJ1dGlvblVuaXF1ZUlkIjogIjUyNGVmOTc2LWMwYmEtZjExMS1hNmE5LTAwMGQzYTU2ZDJmNyIsDQogICJFbWFpbEFkZHJlc3MiOiAiZHB3aWxsaXM2N0BnbWFpbC5jb20iDQp9&hmac=ZHTsuWRFhP0VfE8i9nN_646fEeKx64aFUjBYUEROWWQ=&emci=97af5186-a8ba-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&emdi=524ef976-c0ba-f111-a6a9-000d3a56d2f7&ceid=33603084#/login), at a county election office, or by mail.

clean_body: VoteBeat: Unknown number of Texas voter registrations went unprocessed due to DPS error| | | | | | = Not great news for voters, Team : Just weeks before the pivotal midterm elections, Texas election officials have discovered that an unknown number of voter registration applications have not been processed due to an error by the Texas Department of Public Safety. According to an email sent to county officials and provided to Votebeat, DPS failed to send the applications, which were submitted by voters through its online driver’s license portal, to county voter registrars for processing. This DPS portal is a major voter registration channel in Texas. From 2020 through 2024, about 6 million Texans used it to register to vote, according to testimony DPS officials provided to state lawmakers in 2025. Texas has more than 18 million registered voters. This is where you come in -- if you live in Texas or know someone who does, we have voter tools that you can use. . Voters have until October 5 to update their registrations and can check their status with our tools, on the , at a county election office, or by mail. | | | | | | | | Don't forget: Texas is also cooperating with the Trump administration’s attempts to take control of elections by handing over its voter rolls. If a significant number of Texans are blocked from voting on Election Day because of this registration problem or something else, it could make all the difference in what the Senate looks like for the next six years. = If you've saved your payment information with ActBlue Express, your donation will go through immediately: | | | = | | = | | = | | | = | | = | | = | | | “ A voter who registered through DPS online services but does not appear on the rolls can cast a provisional ballot ,” said Alicia Pierce, a spokesperson for the Texas Secretary of State’s office. This sounds better than it really is. The rates of rejection on provisional ballots are substantially higher than mail-in ballots. ---|---|---
Here's what we're watching in the North Carolina Senate race.
Over the last few weeks, Republicans threw everything they had at Roy Cooper. Not because it was working. Because they needed to find out if anything could move the polls.
Think of it as a test. Pour tens of millions more into TV ads. Make the attacks on Roy Cooper even more outrageous. Send in both Trump and JD Vance. Trump held a[ rally in Gastonia](https://substack.com/redirect/c7f70475-0817-4fbf-a9a3-e5d65735a270?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) with Michael Whatley on Sept. 16th. JD Vance came to[ Greensboro](https://substack.com/redirect/c54e2399-2bd8-4f6a-8a0b-797d13594582?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) five days later. Then check the polls and see if any of it moved the numbers. If it did, spend even more dark money. If it didn't, then cut bait and move the money somewhere they think they can win.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e9452d4c-202b-470c-b5dd-c95aaee71a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
It didn't work. And it looks like they're cutting bait.
A Republican super PAC called Old North Action[ cut $6.5 million in October TV ads](https://substack.com/redirect/3cc36c05-52d7-453a-ba1e-9403e2d64323?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), and[ CNN called it one of the clearest signs yet](https://substack.com/redirect/a0e9472a-1202-4cc4-9df2-d0dcdb44b9d9?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) that Republicans are losing confidence in this race. The main GOP Senate super PAC, Senate Leadership Fund,[ also pulled about $900,000 in broadcast ads](https://substack.com/redirect/3d1ea92d-6cbb-4cc7-a160-6affe934c08e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg).
Why? Because Whatley's numbers didn't move. Cooper is up 11 in the Elon poll and 8 in the ECU poll. He's up 15 in a [poll from the Carolina Journal](https://substack.com/redirect/0d72f472-3d81-47cb-9a39-2942ecddef0e?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), which is not exactly a liberal outfit. The New York Times tracks every poll in this race. Not one has shown Whatley ahead.
Now, they haven't packed up and gone home. Old North Action still has $14.5 million reserved through Election Day, and Senate Leadership Fund has[ $23.2 million](https://substack.com/redirect/3cc36c05-52d7-453a-ba1e-9403e2d64323?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). That's a lot of money still coming at Governor Cooper. But super PACs don't have unlimited cash, and Republican senators have been[ openly debating whether to keep investing here](https://substack.com/redirect/16f2e957-a579-4859-8987-d1a72e951686?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). The first cut usually isn't the last one. If the numbers keep looking like this, more will follow, and they'll move that money to protect Republicans in Texas, Nebraska, Iowa and Kansas.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e9452d4c-202b-470c-b5dd-c95aaee71a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
So what's really going on? Look at the matchup. Roy Cooper spent 16 years as our Attorney General and 8 years as our Governor. That's 24 years working for North Carolina, not for himself. Michael Whatley spent[ more than 15 years lobbying](https://substack.com/redirect/73507a4d-6741-46f3-98b8-081820c9ddb2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) for big oil, then ran the state and national Republican Party. He's never had to answer to North Carolina voters, and his whole record is all about being a partisan hack for Trump.
Michael Whatley is handcuffed to a president who keeps making things worse and making everything cost more. In Gastonia, Trump said North Carolina had become[ "blood-soaked killing fields."](https://substack.com/redirect/6355c338-7125-497f-b14c-afe2a543c217?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) On Helene recovery money, he told the crowd "[if Michael loses, I'm not sending it.](https://substack.com/redirect/13a1e19e-6107-4d2c-b5d9-5c4c62b9026f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)" Folks in western North Carolina are still rebuilding. Calling our state a shit-hole and then threatening to pull hurricane relief funding is a really good way to piss off North Carolinians. And it's not just us. [Trump promised to campaign in 35 of the most competitive races](https://substack.com/redirect/e32f33fa-46cb-426e-b5b7-c38595773ec4?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) this fall. His next rallies? [Alabama and Oklahoma](https://substack.com/redirect/61768c01-f31b-44e2-a8ba-e9c70b96a1fb?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). Not exactly where the close Senate races are.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e9452d4c-202b-470c-b5dd-c95aaee71a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
Here's the part that gets me. Trump's own Attorney General, Todd Blanche, spoke right before him at that rally and [bragged that violent crime in North Carolina fell nearly 11%](https://substack.com/redirect/6355c338-7125-497f-b14c-afe2a543c217?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). And Trump's own FBI data shows North Carolina's violent crime rate was [below the national average last year](https://substack.com/redirect/19f87b06-77f8-4939-aef1-814b77c974e2?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg). By the way, Republicans ran the General Assembly every single year Roy was governor - I know because I served in the state Senate. They wrote the criminal laws and passed budgets that defunded the police and public safety to pay for more tax cuts for billionaires and corporations. I'm about to be your District Attorney and I take public safety seriously. The numbers just don't back up what they're saying about Roy Cooper, and everyone knows it.
Even Trump's own people see it. The [Washington Post reports](https://substack.com/redirect/1959cb6c-753b-4c31-9329-1a5205fb751f?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) his advisers are giving him blunt, grim news about the midterms. And Republicans like Florida Rep. Maria Elvira Salazar are[ cutting ads calling him out](https://substack.com/redirect/d91e402a-c376-4e70-9dca-898b28ee755d?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg), saying Hispanic voters who put him in the White House feel betrayed.
North Carolina is the canary in the coal mine for what we can expect on November 3rd. The first money is already walking out the door. The Cooper campaign still calls this a 50-50 state, and they're right not to take anything for granted. If we keep the pressure on, more of that money leaves, and the whole country takes notice.
| [](https://substack.com/redirect/e9452d4c-202b-470c-b5dd-c95aaee71a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg)|
---|---|---
If you can, [please chip in $10 or $25](https://substack.com/redirect/e9452d4c-202b-470c-b5dd-c95aaee71a50?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) today. We'll split it between Roy's campaign and mine. Republicans have outspent Democrats on ads in this race by about $15 million, so small-dollar contributions make a big difference. And those hard dollars stretch a lot further on TV than super PAC money, because by law candidates get the lowest ad rates. Super PACs can pay two or three times as much for the same spot.
Thanks for reading. Let's finish strong and get Roy Cooper across the finish line.
Wiley

P.S. We've got some very important state level races on the ballot as well. [We're hosting a fundraiser for House Democratic Leader Robert Reives](https://substack.com/redirect/d3384f55-3e2c-4d2e-898e-90f7e0a90d94?j=eyJ1IjoiMWh2cjYwIn0.VBabVq-VHATXCJqsddI7uMpdiTm0WkVanRDZfvCWMkg) at our place in Cary on Thursday October 22nd. Old North Action still has $14.5 million reserved through Election Day, and Senate Leadership Fund has. That's a lot of money still coming at Governor Cooper. But super PACs don't have unlimited cash, and Republican senators have been. The first cut usually isn't the last one. If the numbers keep looking like this, more will follow, and they'll move that money to protect Republicans in Texas, Nebraska, Iowa and Kansas. | | ---|---|--- So what's really going on? Look at the matchup. Roy Cooper spent 16 years as our Attorney General and 8 years as our Governor. That's 24 years working for North Carolina, not for himself. Michael Whatley spent for big oil, then ran the state and national Republican Party. He's never had to answer to North Carolina voters, and his whole record is all about being a partisan hack for Trump. Michael Whatley is handcuffed to a president who keeps making things worse and making everything cost more. They wrote the criminal laws and passed budgets that defunded the police and public safety to pay for more tax cuts for billionaires and corporations. I'm about to be your District Attorney and I take public safety seriously. The numbers just don't back up what they're saying about Roy Cooper, and everyone knows it. Even Trump's own people see it. It's Elaine Luria, and Raja said I could reach out.

On November 8th, 2022, after a difficult, expensive, and hard-fought reelection campaign, I called my opponent to offer my concession and congratulations.
It wasn't a pleasant call to make. But I've never second-guessed the decisions that led me there.
If we haven't met: I entered the Naval Academy at 17 and spent 20 years in the Navy as a nuclear engineer, my entire career aboard combatant ships.
In 2018, I ran for Congress and flipped Virginia's 2nd District.
I'm also a mom, which is still the best job I've ever had.
In Congress, I served on the January 6th Committee, knowing full well it could cost me my seat. That cycle, outside far-right groups spent $6,059,677 against me. Add a national environment that was brutal for frontline Democrats, and I came up short.
_**For me, the worst outcome isn’t losing a fight. It’s going down with no fight at all.**_
So I'm back, running to win this seat back from Jen Kiggans, because I can't sit on the sidelines and watch our country descend into chaos.
The Cook Political Report rates VA-02 a Toss-Up. This is one of Democrats’ best pickup opportunities in the country.
Republicans know it too. Jen Kiggans called Elon Musk's DOGE cuts "so necessary," even as they hit Hampton Roads hard. Now Musk's super PAC has started spending to keep her in office and beat me.
That's why September 30th matters. It's my last end-of-quarter FEC deadline before Election Day, and the report that follows is public. Reporters, national groups, and Kiggans' allies will all read it to decide how seriously to take this race.

**Yesterday was National Public Lands Day, Peter.**

There are few things I love more about Washington than the feeling of being outside here—surrounded by our mountains, forests, rivers, and trails.

These places hold so many of our memories. They're where we take our kids for their first hike, spend quiet mornings on the water, and remember just how lucky we are to call this place home.

Since he took office, Donald Trump has made devastating changes to public lands. He's working to eliminate protections for 2 million acres of roadless national forest land in Washington. He shrank Utah's Bears Ears National Monument and Grand Staircase-Escalante National Monument and opened those ecosystems back up to the mining industry. He's accelerating oil-and-gas leasing on federal lands. And now he wants to change the default from “no motorized vehicles” to “motorized vehicles allowed” unless signs are posted on the thousands of trails we treasure.

**Trump's actions are a reminder that the places we love will remain safe and protected ONLY if we choose to care for them.**

Once a forest is gone, a habitat is destroyed, or a treasured landscape is fundamentally changed, we can't put it back the way it was. We have a responsibility to preserve these beautiful places for generations to come. That responsibility means a great deal to me, and I'll keep doing everything I can to protect the public lands that make Washington home.

I hope you'll take a moment to appreciate them, get outside, and fight for them, too.

Kim Rep. Kim Schrier is a doctor, scientist, and mom, fighting for Washington's 8th District in Congress. I learned something this week that stopped me in my tracks. I don’t ask for help easily. I was raised to do the hard thing, keep my faith, and keep moving. But what I learned about what is being coordinated against this fight — how deep it goes, how certain they are that they can overwhelm us — made me stop. I thought about every person who has shown up for this movement. Every parent, every small business owner, every hardworking American who gave something real because they believed it would matter. And I thought: they deserve the truth.
